title: Dutch Beef Stew
intro: Meltingly tender beef, sweet carrots and potatoes in a gently tangy gravy: Dutch winter comfort food that fills the whole house with the most wonderful smell.

ingredients.item: braising beef (chuck), cut into 4 cm chunks
ingredients.es: carne para guisar (morcillo o aguja de ternera)
ingredients.swap: pork shoulder (aguja) instead of beef

steps: Dust the meat with flour, salt and pepper. Brown it all over in hot oil in two batches; this gives you flavour and a nicely thickened gravy.
Cut the potatoes and carrots into large chunks and put them in the bottom of the slow cooker, where it's hottest. Lay the meat on top.
Soften the onions in the same pan for 3 minutes. Deglaze with the stock, mustard, vinegar and sugar, scraping up all the browned bits.
Pour this over the meat, tuck in the bay leaves and put the lid on. Cook for 8–9 hours on LOW or 5–6 hours on HIGH.
Fish out the bay leaves and taste: season with salt, pepper and an extra splash of vinegar if you like. The meat should fall apart.
tip: Choose waxy potatoes and cut them into large chunks so they hold their shape. Gravy too thin? Mash a few pieces of potato and stir them in: free thickening.
kids: Mash the meat, potato and carrot together with a little gravy: a familiar Dutch-style stamppot for little eaters.

title: Spanish Lentils with Chorizo
intro: This is how all of Spain eats on a weeknight: a thick, smoky lentil stew you'll want to mop up with a hunk of bread.
steps: Rinse the lentils in a sieve until the water runs clear; there's no need to soak them. Peel the potatoes and carrots and cut them into 2 cm cubes.
Fry the chorizo in the olive oil for 2 minutes, then add the onion and garlic and soften for 3 minutes. Take the pan off the heat before stirring in the paprika; it burns quickly.
Tip everything into the slow cooker with the lentils, vegetables, passata, bay leaf and stock. Don't add salt yet: you'll do that at the end.
Cook with the lid on for 6–7 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH, until the lentils are completely soft.
Too thick? Stir in a little hot water. Remove the bay leaf and season with salt, pepper and the vinegar.
tip: Squash a few cubes of potato against the side of the pot and stir them in: the stew turns creamy all by itself. A splash of sherry vinegar at the end deepens the flavour, just the way Spanish grandmothers do it.
kids: Always choose chorizo dulce, never picante. Spice lovers can sprinkle a little pimentón picante over their own plate.

title: Creamy Chicken with Peppers and Rice
intro: Tender chicken thighs in a velvety, sweet pepper and cream sauce packed with vegetables: colourful on the plate and a guaranteed hit.

ingredients.item: boneless chicken thighs, cut into large pieces
peppers (red and yellow), cut into strips

steps: Season the chicken with salt, pepper and half the paprika. Brown the pieces quickly in oil until golden; they don't need to be cooked through yet.
Put the carrot and onion in the bottom of the slow cooker, then the peppers, mushrooms (optional) and chicken. Mix the stock, tomato purée, remaining paprika and oregano and pour it over the top.
Cook with the lid on for 4–5 hours on LOW or 2–3 hours on HIGH. The chicken is done when it reaches 75 °C in the centre.
For the last half hour, stir in the cooking cream (optional) and the cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp cold water. Put the lid back on and let it carry on cooking.
Meanwhile, cook the rice according to the packet instructions and spoon the chicken and sauce over the top.
tip: That little spoonful of tomato purée is my secret: it gives the pepper sauce depth and a warm colour without tasting of tomato.
kids: Not keen on mushrooms? Chop them very finely and they'll disappear into the sauce unnoticed.

title: Meatballs in Italian Tomato Sauce
intro: Juicy meatballs that simmer gently for hours in a sweet tomato sauce with hidden vegetables: a treat for every child.
steps: Briefly mix the mince, egg, breadcrumbs, Parmesan (optional), 1 tsp Italian herbs, salt and pepper. With wet hands, roll into about 20 meatballs.
Brown the meatballs all over in olive oil. They don't need to be cooked through; the crust adds flavour and helps them hold together.
Stir the passata, tomato purée, onion, carrot (optional), garlic, oregano and the rest of the herbs together in the slow cooker. Swirl the 100 ml water round the passata carton and add it too.
Add the meatballs to the sauce and gently spoon it over them. Cook for 4–5 hours on LOW or 2–3 hours on HIGH.
Cook the spaghetti until al dente, season the sauce with salt and pepper to taste and serve with an extra sprinkle of Parmesan (optional).
tip: Mix the mince as little as possible: the less you work it, the more tender the meatballs. They're done when they're no longer pink inside.
kids: Let the children roll the meatballs themselves; homemade tastes twice as good. Grown-ups: chilli flakes at the table.

title: Pulled Chicken Wraps
intro: Sweet, smoky chicken that falls apart all on its own: roll your own wraps at the table and watch how fast the dish empties.
steps: Stir the passata, tomato purée, honey (optional), mustard, vinegar, paprika and garlic powder together with salt and pepper in the slow cooker.
Add the onion and lay the chicken on top. Spoon the sauce over the chicken so everything is covered.
Cook with the lid on for 4–5 hours on LOW or 2–3 hours on HIGH, until the chicken reaches 75 °C and pulls apart easily.
Shred the chicken with two forks right in the pot and stir it through the sauce. Too runny? Leave the lid off and let it thicken on HIGH for 20 minutes.
Warm the wraps briefly in a dry frying pan. Everyone fills their own with chicken, sweetcorn, cucumber and a spoonful of yoghurt (optional).
tip: Use chicken thighs, not breast: thigh stays juicy and shreds beautifully, while breast turns dry and stringy. Leftovers are delicious in a toastie the next day.
kids: Let the children roll their own wraps. Grown-ups: a few drops of Tabasco or some jalapeño.

title: Bolognese with Extra Vegetables
intro: A rich, deeply tomatoey bolognese in which courgette, carrot and celery quietly vanish: vegetables eaten without anyone noticing.

ingredients.swap: replace half the mince with red lentils

steps: Fry the mince in olive oil in a hot pan until browned and crumbly. Leave it alone for a moment before stirring; that's how you get those flavourful crispy bits.
Finely chop the onion and celery (optional) and coarsely grate the carrot and courgette (optional). The finer they are, the less likely the children are to spot them.
Put the mince, vegetables, passata, tomato purée, stock, herbs and bay leaf in the slow cooker. Stir well and season with salt and pepper.
Cook for 6–7 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH. Too runny? Leave the lid slightly ajar for the last 30 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf, cook the spaghetti until al dente and spoon the sauce generously over the top.
tip: Just before serving, stir a splash of pasta cooking water into the sauce: it turns glossy and clings to the spaghetti better. A true Italian trick.
kids: Give the sauce a quick blitz with a stick blender: silky smooth, and the vegetables become invisible.

title: Mild Chilli con Carne
intro: A warm, deep-flavoured chilli without the fiery edge: comfort food that has children asking for seconds.

ingredients.item: mince (beef or mixed beef and pork)
ingredients.swap: replace half the mince with red lentils

steps: Fry the mince in oil over a high heat until browned and crumbly; let it really colour, because that's where the flavour is. Add the onion, pepper and garlic and fry for 3 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the paprika, cumin and tomato purée and tip everything into the slow cooker.
Add the passata, stock and rinsed kidney beans. Season with salt and pepper, stir and put the lid on.
Cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3 hours on HIGH. Stir in the sweetcorn (optional) for the last half hour so it stays crunchy.
Meanwhile, cook the rice. Taste the chilli, adjust the seasoning and serve.
tip: Always use tinned or jarred kidney beans: dried ones don't get hot enough in a slow cooker to be safe. And feel free to make it a day ahead; chilli tastes even better the next day.
kids: Children eat it just as it is; grown-ups sprinkle chilli flakes or jalapeño over their own plate.

title: Spanish Chicken and Chickpea Stew
intro: Golden chicken, creamy chickpeas and sweet paprika in a tomato sauce that smells like an Andalusian village kitchen.

ingredients.item: boneless chicken thighs, cut into large pieces
ingredients.swap: bone-in chicken legs instead of thigh fillets

steps: Season the chicken with salt and pepper and fry in olive oil for 3–4 minutes until golden; it doesn't need to be cooked through yet.
Soften the onion and garlic in the same oil for 3 minutes. Take the pan off the heat and stir in the paprika, cumin and oregano.
Put the potato and carrot (in 2 cm cubes) in the bottom of the slow cooker, then add the rinsed chickpeas, chicken and onion. Pour the passata and stock over the top.
Cook with the lid on for 4–5 hours on LOW or 2–3 hours on HIGH, until the potato is soft and the chicken reaches 75 °C.
Taste and season with salt and pepper. Too runny? Mash a spoonful of chickpeas and stir them in.
tip: Potato and carrot go at the bottom: that's where the slow cooker is hottest, and hard vegetables need the most time. Rinse the chickpeas well; the liquid from the jar tastes salty and dull.
kids: Mild and soft, perfect for mashing. Grown-ups: a pinch of pimentón picante at the table.

title: Potato and Leek Soup
intro: A velvety, creamy leek and potato soup: simple, inexpensive and just what you want on a crisp autumn evening.
steps: Slice the leeks into rings and rinse them well in a colander: there's often sand hiding between the layers. Chop the onion.
Gently soften the leek and onion in the butter for 5 minutes without letting them colour. This gives the soup a sweet, rounded flavour.
Put the leek, onion, potato and stock in the slow cooker, filling it no more than three-quarters full. Cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH.
Blend the soup until smooth with a stick blender. Keep the head below the surface and it won't splatter.
Stir in the cooking cream (optional) and let it warm through for 10 minutes. Season with salt, pepper and a pinch of nutmeg.
tip: Blend only briefly: over-blending makes potato gluey. Freezing it? Do so before adding the cream, then stir the cream in after reheating.
kids: Serve with strips of cheesy toast for dipping into the soup.

title: Mild Coconut Chicken Curry
intro: A velvety, golden curry with a sweet hint of apple: the curry that will make your children fall in love with world cooking.

ingredients.item: boneless chicken thighs, cut into pieces

steps: Soften the onion in oil for 3 minutes, then stir in the curry powder and garlic powder for 30 seconds until fragrant. This cooks out the raw taste of the spices.
Put the chicken, carrot, pepper (optional) and apple (optional) in the slow cooker. Spoon the curried onion over the top, pour in half the coconut milk and add salt.
Cook with the lid on for 4–5 hours on LOW or 2–3 hours on HIGH, until the chicken reaches 75 °C.
For the last half hour, stir in the rest of the coconut milk and the cornflour mixed with the cold water. Switch to HIGH and keep the lid on until the sauce thickens.
Meanwhile, cook the rice, taste the curry for salt and serve.
tip: Spices only really release their flavour in hot oil, so always fry the curry powder briefly. Adding the second half of the coconut milk at the end makes the sauce extra creamy and fresh.
kids: The apple gives the sauce a gentle sweetness. Grown-ups: sambal or chilli flakes at the table.

title: Moroccan Chicken Stew with Ras el Hanout
intro: Cinnamon, ras el hanout and sweet apricots fill your kitchen with the scent of a Moroccan souk.

ingredients.item: boneless chicken thighs, cut into large pieces

steps: Season the chicken with salt and fry in olive oil for 3 minutes. Add the onion and garlic to soften, then stir in the ras el hanout and cinnamon for 30 seconds.
Put the carrot, chickpeas, apricots (optional) and chicken mixture in the slow cooker. Pour the passata and stock over the top.
Cook with the lid on for 4–5 hours on LOW or 2–3 hours on HIGH, until the chicken reaches 75 °C.
Optional: For the last hour, lay the courgette on top and quickly put the lid back on; that way it stays whole and nicely green.
Pour the boiling stock over the couscous, cover and leave to swell for 5 minutes, then fluff it up with a fork.
tip: Ras el hanout varies from brand to brand: some are sweet and floral, others punchy. Give it a sniff, start with 1 tablespoon and feel free to stir in a little extra at the end.
kids: The apricots make it soft and sweet. Grown-ups: a little spoonful of harissa on their own plate.

title: Dutch Braised Beef with Mash
intro: Draadjesvlees just like Grandma used to make: beef so tender it falls into threads, in a glossy sweet-and-sour gravy, with a mountain of creamy mash on the side.

ingredients.item: braising beef (blade or chuck), cut into chunks
ingredients.swap: pork shoulder (aguja) instead of beef

steps: Pat the meat dry, season with salt and pepper and brown it in small batches in oil until deep brown all over. Transfer it to the slow cooker.
Fry the onions in the same pan until golden. Deglaze with the stock, mustard, vinegar and sugar, scraping up all the browned bits.
Pour this over the meat, add the carrot (optional), bay leaves and thyme and put the lid on. Cook for 8–9 hours on LOW or 5–6 hours on HIGH.
For the last half hour, stir the cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp cold water into the gravy. Fish out the bay leaves and thyme stalks.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes until tender, drain and mash with the warm milk, butter and salt until creamy.
tip: Deep browning is everything: work in small batches, otherwise the meat stews instead of colouring. Want it extra Dutch? Add 2 whole cloves.
kids: Make a little well in the mash and fill it with gravy: a gravy volcano. Children love it.

title: Pulled Pork Tacos
intro: Slow-cooked pork shoulder in a sticky, smoky sauce: set up a taco bar on the table and let everyone build their own.
steps: Cut the meat into 4 large pieces and rub them with the paprika, cumin, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Put the onion in the bottom of the slow cooker and the meat on top. Mix the passata, tomato purée, honey (optional) and vinegar and pour over the meat.
Cook with the lid on for 8–9 hours on LOW or 5–6 hours on HIGH, until the meat falls apart with a fork.
Lift out the meat, shred it and discard any large pieces of fat. Reduce the sauce in a pan for 5–10 minutes until syrupy.
Stir the meat through the reduced sauce. Warm the tortillas briefly in a dry frying pan and fill them at the table with the toppings.
tip: Shoulder has just the right amount of fat and connective tissue to turn meltingly tender; lean cuts such as lomo dry out. Reducing the sauce is the difference between good and great.
kids: Children choose their own toppings. Grown-ups: jalapeño, salsa picante or a wedge of lime.

title: Creamy Mild Chicken Tikka Masala
intro: The creamy orange curry from your favourite Indian restaurant, but gentle enough for the whole table.

ingredients.item: boneless chicken thighs, cut into 3 cm cubes

steps: Soften the onion, garlic and ginger in oil for 4 minutes. Stir in all the spices and the tomato purée and fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Put the chicken in the slow cooker, spoon the spice mixture and passata over it, add salt and stir.
Cook with the lid on for 4–5 hours on LOW or 2–3 hours on HIGH, until the chicken reaches 75 °C.
For the last 15 minutes, stir in the cooking cream. Then switch the slow cooker off or to WARM.
Optional: Mix the yoghurt with a few spoonfuls of the hot sauce and only then stir it into the curry. Don't let it boil again, or it will split.
Cook the basmati rice separately and serve.
tip: Full-fat yoghurt is far less likely to split than low-fat, and 'tempering' it with warm sauce first prevents lumps. Ground ginger works too: use 1 teaspoon instead of fresh. Freezing it? Do so before adding the cream and yoghurt.
kids: Creamy and mild. Grown-ups: chilli flakes or a finely chopped green chilli on top.

title: Chicken in Creamy Mushroom Sauce
intro: Tender chicken in a creamy sauce with mushrooms, garlic and thyme: comfort food that tastes as if you'd spent hours in the kitchen.
steps: Season the chicken with salt and pepper, brown it quickly in oil until golden and transfer it to the slow cooker.
Fry the mushrooms, onion and garlic in the same pan over a high heat for 4 minutes. This drives off the mushrooms' water and gives them flavour.
Spoon this over the chicken, pour in the stock and sprinkle over the thyme. Cook for 4–5 hours on LOW or 2–3 hours on HIGH.
For the last half hour, stir in the cooking cream and the cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp cold water. The chicken must reach 75 °C in the centre.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes and mash them with the milk and butter. Sprinkle the parsley (optional) over the chicken and serve.
tip: Fry the mushrooms over a high heat and not too many at once, so they brown rather than stew. That's the difference between a bland sauce and a rich one.
kids: Mash the potato with a spoonful of sauce: creamy, mild and easy to eat for little hands.

title: Pork in Honey Mustard Sauce
intro: Tender braised pork with apple in a sweet, creamy honey mustard sauce: the perfect balance of sweet and savoury.

ingredients.item: pork shoulder, cut into 4 cm chunks
ingredients.es: aguja o paleta de cerdo para guisar

steps: Trim any excess fat from the meat. Season with salt and pepper and lightly brown the chunks in oil in batches.
Put the carrot, onion and apple (optional) in the bottom of the slow cooker and spoon the meat on top.
Mix the stock, honey, 1 tbsp mustard and the thyme and pour it over. Cook for 6–7 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH.
For the last half hour, stir in the cooking cream (optional), the rest of the mustard and the cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp cold water.
Meanwhile, cook the potatoes or rice. Taste the sauce and season with salt, pepper or an extra spoonful of honey.
tip: Mustard loses its punch during long cooking. That's why you add half of it only at the end: the sauce stays fresh and you can really taste the mustard.
kids: Too mustardy? An extra splash of cream and a little honey will soften the sauce for little tasters.

title: Cottage Pie with Mince and Vegetables
intro: A savoury mince and vegetable filling under a blanket of creamy mash: British comfort food that gets the whole family to the table.

ingredients.swap: replace half the mince with red lentils

steps: Fry the mince and onion in oil until browned and crumbly. Spoon into the slow cooker with the carrot, passata, tomato purée, stock, thyme and Worcestershire sauce.
Season with salt and pepper and cook with the lid on for 4–5 hours on LOW or 2–3 hours on HIGH.
For the last half hour, stir in the peas (optional) and the cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp cold water. This thickens the filling nicely.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes and mash them with the milk, butter and salt to a firm mash.
Spoon the filling into an ovenproof dish, spread the mash over the top and rough it up with a fork. Place under a hot grill for 10 minutes (or 15 min at 220 °C) until golden.
tip: The fork ridges turn into crispy edges under the grill: the best bit. No grill? Spoon the mash over the filling in the slow cooker and heat through for 15 minutes.
kids: Sprinkle some grated cheese over the mash: everyone will want a piece of the golden crust.

title: Tuscan Chicken
intro: Creamy chicken with sun-dried tomatoes, spinach and Parmesan: it tastes like an Italian holiday, even on an ordinary weeknight.

ingredients.item: sun-dried tomatoes in oil, cut into strips

steps: Season the chicken with salt, pepper and oregano and brown it quickly in oil until golden. Feel free to use the oil from the tomato jar.
Put the onion and garlic in the bottom of the slow cooker, then the chicken and sun-dried tomatoes (optional). Pour the stock over the top.
Cook with the lid on for 3½–4 hours on LOW or 2 hours on HIGH, until the chicken reaches 75 °C in the centre.
For the last half hour, stir in the cooking cream and the cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp cold water.
10 minutes before the end, stir in the spinach and Parmesan (optional); the spinach wilts by itself. Meanwhile, cook the pasta and serve.
tip: Sun-dried tomatoes in oil are softer and fuller in flavour than the dry ones from a packet. Only got those? Soak them in hot water for 10 minutes first.
kids: Spinach sceptics? Chop the leaves finely and they become inconspicuous green flecks in the sauce.

title: Mexican Pulled Beef
intro: Beef that falls into shreds after a day of simmering, with cumin, oregano and a fresh squeeze of lime.

ingredients.swap: pork shoulder instead of beef shoulder

steps: Cut the meat into 4 pieces, season with salt and pepper and brown well all over in oil, 6–8 minutes. That crust is pure flavour.
Put the onion and pepper in the bottom of the slow cooker and the meat on top.
Mix the passata, stock, garlic, cumin, paprika and oregano and pour over the meat.
Cook with the lid on for 8–9 hours on LOW or 5–6 hours on HIGH, until the meat falls apart with a fork.
Shred the meat in the pot, stir it through the sauce and squeeze over the lime juice. Serve in warm tortillas.
tip: Add the lime only at the end so it stays fresh. Leftovers? Freeze portions with a little sauce: perfect for quesadillas or a quick burrito bowl.
kids: Mild and smoky. Grown-ups: jalapeño, salsa picante or a pinch of cayenne at the table.

title: Teriyaki Chicken
intro: Glossy, sweet-and-salty chicken with ginger and garlic: within a week, everyone will be asking for it.
steps: Stir the soy sauce, honey, water, vinegar, garlic and ginger together in the slow cooker.
Add the chicken thighs, whole or in large pieces, and spoon the sauce over them. Put the lid on.
Cook for 4 hours on LOW or 2 hours on HIGH, until the chicken reaches 75 °C.
Mix the cornflour with the cold water and stir it into the sauce. Switch to HIGH and leave with the lid on for 20–30 minutes until thickened and glossy.
Slice or shred the chicken, stir it through the sauce and serve on rice, sprinkled with sesame seeds (optional).
tip: Chicken thigh stays juicy and soaks up the sauce better than breast. Too salty for the children? Use reduced-salt soy sauce or replace 2 tablespoons of it with water.
kids: Sweet, salty and sticky: a children's favourite. Grown-ups: sriracha or chilli flakes on the side.

title: Thai Coconut Chicken with Peanut Sauce
intro: Creamy coconut, nutty peanut and a fresh squeeze of lime: a Thai street-food night, straight from your own slow cooker.

ingredients.item: boneless chicken thighs, cut into pieces

steps: Soften the onion in oil for 3 minutes and stir in the curry powder for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Put the chicken, pepper (optional), carrot and curried onion in the slow cooker. Pour over half the coconut milk and the soy sauce.
Cook with the lid on for 4 hours on LOW or 2 hours on HIGH, until the chicken reaches 75 °C.
For the last half hour, whisk the rest of the coconut milk with the peanut butter until smooth and stir it into the stew. Lid on, for another 20–30 minutes.
Stir in the lime juice, taste for salt and serve with rice.
tip: Whisk the peanut butter into cold coconut milk first: that way it dissolves without lumps and won't catch on the bottom. Add the lime only at the end so it stays fresh.
kids: Creamy and nutty. Watch out for peanut allergies among visiting friends! Grown-ups: sambal on the side.

title: Greek Lemon Chicken with Potatoes
intro: Sunny chicken with lemon, garlic and oregano on potatoes that soak up all the juices: a Greek summer terrace on a weeknight.

ingredients.swap: bone-in chicken legs instead of thigh fillets

steps: Cut the potatoes into 3 cm wedges and put them in the bottom of the slow cooker with the onion, garlic, salt and pepper.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper. If you like, brown it in a hot pan for 3 minutes: it gives a nicer colour and a fuller flavour.
Lay the chicken on the potatoes. Whisk the lemon juice, olive oil, stock, oregano and thyme together and pour over.
Cook with the lid on for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3 hours on HIGH, until the potatoes are soft and the chicken reaches 75 °C.
Just before serving, grate the lemon zest over the top and spoon the juices through the potatoes. Serve with yoghurt (optional) and cucumber (optional).
tip: Only zest the lemon at the end: hours of cooking dull its flavour, while fresh zest makes everything sing. Want crispy edges? Pop the potatoes under the grill for another 10 minutes.
kids: Too sour for the little ones? Use half a lemon and give the grown-ups extra zest.

title: Creamy Tomato Fish Stew
intro: Tender hake gently cooked in a creamy tomato and pepper sauce: fish that wins over even the doubters at the table.

ingredients.swap: frozen hake or coley instead of fresh

ingredients.es: nata para cocinar / leche de coco

steps: Put the chopped onion and garlic, pepper, carrot, passata, stock, oil, paprika, oregano, salt and pepper in the slow cooker.
Cook with the lid on for 3–4 hours on LOW or 1½–2 hours on HIGH, until the vegetables are soft.
Stir in the cream or coconut milk (optional). Pat the fish dry, cut it into 4 cm pieces, season with salt and gently lay them in the sauce.
Put the lid on and cook for 20–30 minutes on LOW (15–20 on HIGH), until the fish is white and just flakes apart. Don't stir.
Meanwhile, cook the rice. Carefully spoon the fish and sauce onto the plates.
tip: Frozen hake is cheap and perfectly good: defrost it overnight in the fridge and pat it thoroughly dry. Check after 15 minutes on HIGH or 20 on LOW, because overcooking makes fish dry.
kids: Check for small bones before serving. Grown-ups: a pinch of pimentón picante on top.

title: Creamy Garlic Prawns with Pasta
intro: Sweet slow-cooked garlic, a creamy sauce and juicy prawns tossed through your pasta: a restaurant feel at a bargain price.
steps: Gently soften the onion and garlic in olive oil for 3 minutes without letting them colour. Put them in the slow cooker with the stock and paprika.
Cook with the lid on for 2–3 hours on LOW or 1–1½ hours on HIGH, until the onion and garlic are soft and sweet.
Pat the defrosted prawns thoroughly dry. Meanwhile, cook the pasta and save a cup of the cooking water.
Switch the slow cooker to HIGH and stir in the cream and prawns. Lid on, 10–15 minutes, until they're pink and just cooked.
Stir in the lemon juice, parsley (optional), salt and pepper and toss the pasta through. Too thick? Add a splash of the cooking water.
tip: Choose raw prawns; pre-cooked ones quickly turn rubbery and only need 5 minutes. A C shape means perfectly cooked, a tight O shape means they've gone too long.
kids: Not a prawn fan? Dish up their pasta first with just the creamy sauce.

title: Spanish Cod and Potato Stew
intro: Pearly white cod on a bed of potato, pepper and tomato, drizzled with good olive oil: pure Spanish home cooking.

ingredients.swap: frozen hake or coley instead of bacalao

steps: Cut the potatoes into 1 cm slices and lay them in the bottom of the slow cooker. Scatter the onion, garlic and pepper over the top.
Mix the passata, stock, 2 tbsp oil and paprika, pour it over and season lightly with salt. Cook for 3–4 hours on LOW or 2 hours on HIGH.
Are the potatoes soft? Pat the fish dry, cut it into 5 cm pieces and lay them on top. Drizzle with the remaining oil.
Put the lid on and cook for 20–30 minutes on LOW (15–20 on HIGH), until the fish is pearly white and separates into flakes.
Scatter over the olives (optional), only now taste for salt, and serve with bread to mop up the sauce.
tip: Desalting it yourself? Soak the bacalao in cold water in the fridge for 24–36 hours, changing the water 3–4 times. Easier: frozen 'bacalao desalado', or simply fresh cod.
kids: Check for bones and serve the fish with some potato. Olives only for those who like them.

title: Mild Coconut Prawn Curry
intro: A soft yellow coconut curry with juicy prawns and a fresh squeeze of lime: a holiday in a bowl, ready in no time.
steps: Soften the onion, garlic and ginger in oil for 3 minutes and stir in the curry powder for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Put the mixture in the slow cooker with the carrot and pepper (optional). Pour over the coconut milk, add salt and stir.
Cook with the lid on for 2–3 hours on LOW or 1–1½ hours on HIGH, until the vegetables are soft.
Switch to HIGH and stir in the prawns, patted dry. Lid on, 10–15 minutes, until they're pink and just cooked.
Stir in the lime juice, taste for salt and serve straight away with rice.
tip: Prawns go from juicy to tough in a matter of minutes: have the rice ready before they go in and serve immediately. Full-fat coconut milk gives the richest sauce.
kids: A soft, creamy curry. Grown-ups: sambal or chilli flakes at the table.

title: Spanish Chorizo and Potato Stew
intro: Patatas a la riojana for the whole family: potatoes that melt into a deep red, smoky sauce full of chorizo.
steps: Peel the potatoes and 'break' them into 3 cm pieces: cut halfway in, then prise them apart. Those rough edges will thicken the sauce later.
Fry the chorizo in the oil for 3 minutes until it releases its red fat. Add the onion and garlic and soften for 3 minutes; take the pan off the heat and stir in the paprika.
Put the potato and carrot in the slow cooker, spoon the chorizo mixture over the top and add the passata, stock and bay leaves. The liquid should come to just below the top of the potatoes.
Cook with the lid on for 6–7 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH, until the potatoes are soft.
Squash a few pieces of potato against the side for a thicker sauce. Remove the bay leaves and only now add salt: chorizo is salty already.
tip: 'Breaking' the potatoes (chascar, as the Spanish say) releases starch that thickens the sauce, no flour needed. If a lot of fat floats to the top, skim it off with a spoon before serving.
kids: Cut the chorizo into small half-moons; children love spearing them between the potatoes.

title: Creamy Tomato and Lentil Soup
intro: A thick, creamy soup full of red lentils and tomato: nourishing, dirt cheap and ready to go in ten minutes.
steps: Rinse the lentils in a sieve under cold water until the water runs clear. This prevents foam and a floury taste.
Put the lentils, passata, onion, carrot, stock, cumin and paprika in the slow cooker and stir well.
Cook for 6 hours on LOW or 3 hours on HIGH. The red lentils break down by themselves and thicken the soup.
Blend the soup until smooth or leave it nice and chunky. Too thick? Stir in a splash of hot water.
Stir in the cooking cream (optional) and lemon juice, heat through for 5 minutes and season with salt and pepper. Drizzle each bowl with olive oil.
tip: That little bit of lemon juice at the end is my secret: it suddenly makes the earthy lentils fresh and lively. Lentils keep thickening as they stand, so thin any leftovers with a little water.
kids: Serve with a swirl of cream and some baguette for dunking. Grown-ups: chilli flakes at the table.

title: Old-Fashioned Chicken and Vegetable Stew
intro: An honest, old-fashioned stew of tender chicken, potatoes and carrots in a thickened gravy: one pot, everything in, everyone happy.

ingredients.item: boneless chicken thighs, cut into large pieces
ingredients.swap: bone-in chicken legs instead of thigh fillets

steps: Cut the potatoes and carrots into rough 3 cm chunks and put them in the bottom of the slow cooker. That's where it's hottest.
Season the chicken with salt, pepper and thyme and brown it quickly in oil until golden. Add the onions and fry for 2 minutes.
Lay the chicken and onion on the vegetables, pour over the stock and add the bay leaves. Fill the pot no more than three-quarters full.
Cook with the lid on for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3 hours on HIGH, until the potatoes are soft and the chicken reaches 75 °C.
For the last half hour, stir in the cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp cold water. Fish out the bay leaves and serve.
tip: Chicken thigh stays juicy during long cooking, while breast dries out. Cut the pieces large so they don't fall apart. A scattering of fresh parsley adds colour.
kids: Mash the potato and carrot with a little gravy into a stamppot: easy and familiar.

title: Italian Mince and Vegetable Stew
intro: A colourful, rustic stew of mince and chunky vegetables in tomato sauce: delicious with pasta and rice alike, and kind to your budget.

ingredients.swap: replace half the mince with red lentils

steps: Fry the mince with the onion and garlic in olive oil until browned and crumbly. Season with salt and pepper.
Put the carrot in the bottom of the slow cooker and spoon the mince on top.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes, stock and herbs. Lay the courgette on top; that way it stays firmer.
Cook with the lid on for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3 hours on HIGH.
Give everything a stir and taste. Meanwhile, cook the pasta or rice and spoon the stew generously over the top.
tip: Leftovers? The next day, spoon them into an ovenproof dish, sprinkle with cheese and bake for 15 minutes at 200 °C: a free oven bake.
kids: Choose small pasta shapes and cut the courgette smaller: easy spooning for little eaters.

title: Spanish Meatballs with Carrots and Peas
intro: Tender little meatballs in a gentle Spanish gravy with carrots and peas: a tapas classic that works every bit as well as a family meal.

ingredients.es: carne picada mixta cerdo y vacuno

steps: Mix the mince, egg, soaked breadcrumbs, half the garlic, a little parsley, salt and pepper. With wet hands, roll into about 20 meatballs.
Roll them in 1 tbsp flour and brown them all over in olive oil in batches; they don't need to be cooked through yet. Put them in the slow cooker.
Soften the onion, carrot and the rest of the garlic in the same pan for 4 minutes. Sprinkle over the remaining flour, deglaze with the wine (optional) and let it bubble for 2 minutes.
Stir in the stock, scrape up the browned bits and pour the sauce over the meatballs. Cook for 4–5 hours on LOW or 2–3 hours on HIGH.
Stir in the peas (optional) for the last half hour. Taste the sauce; the meatballs are done when they are no longer pink inside.
tip: Blend a few carrot slices with a little sauce and stir it back in: the gravy turns creamy all by itself, just like in the tapas bar round the corner.
kids: Let them help roll the meatballs; with white rice and a spoonful of sauce, everything disappears.

title: Pork Cheeks in Red Wine with Mash
intro: Pork cheeks that fall apart at the touch of a fork after a day in red wine: Andalusian Sunday lunch, with creamy mash on the side.

ingredients.swap: pork shoulder (aguja) instead of cheeks

ingredients.item: bay leaves and a sprig of thyme
floury potatoes, plus a splash of milk and a knob of butter for the mash

serve.item: bread to mop up the sauce

steps: Pat the cheeks dry, dust them with flour, salt and pepper and brown them all over in olive oil in batches. Put them in the slow cooker.
Soften the onion, carrot, pepper (optional) and garlic in the same pan for 5 minutes. Stir in the tomato purée and fry for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble hard for 3–4 minutes: almost nothing evaporates in a slow cooker, so the alcohol needs to cook off now.
Add the stock, bay leaves and thyme, scrape the pan clean and pour everything over the meat. Cook for 8–9 hours on LOW or 5–6 hours on HIGH.
Lift out the meat, fish out the bay leaves and thyme and blend the vegetables and juices into a glossy sauce. Return the cheeks to the pot.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes until tender and mash them with warm milk and a knob of butter until smooth and creamy.
tip: Ask at the meat counter for 'carrilleras ibéricas': even more tender. Rather go without wine? Use grape juice with a splash of vinegar, or simply extra stock.
kids: The meat falls apart with a fork; mash it into the potato with a spoonful of sauce.

title: Mild Garlic Chicken with Baby Potatoes
intro: Chicken with whole garlic cloves, white wine and baby potatoes: the Spanish classic, but slow-cooked so it turns soft, sweet and mild.

ingredients.swap: bone-in chicken legs instead of thigh fillets

steps: Put the baby potatoes in the bottom of the slow cooker, where it's hottest. Dust the chicken with flour, salt and pepper and brown it on both sides until golden.
Gently fry the whole garlic cloves alongside for 2 minutes until pale golden; if they brown they turn bitter. Lay the chicken and garlic on top of the potatoes.
Deglaze the pan with the wine (optional), let it reduce for 2 minutes and add the stock, bay leaf and thyme. Pour this over the chicken.
Cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH. The chicken is done when it reaches 75 °C in the thickest part.
Stir in the lemon juice and parsley (optional) and taste. Anyone who likes heat can sprinkle a little guindilla (dried chilli flakes) over their own plate at the table.
tip: Slow-cooked whole cloves turn sweet and soft: mash them into the sauce or spread them on bread. That's what makes this ajillo surprisingly mild.
kids: The garlic is soft and sweet; serve the chicken and potatoes with a spoonful of sauce and some bread.

title: Light Asturian Bean Stew with Mild Chorizo
intro: Creamy white beans with mild chorizo and saffron: a lighter, quicker fabada from Asturias, perfect for a cool winter evening on the coast.

ingredients.es: caldo de pollo bajo en sal

steps: Fry the chorizo and diced ham (optional) in olive oil for 3 minutes until the fat turns red. Add the onion, carrot and garlic and soften for 4 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the paprika so it doesn't burn. Put everything in the slow cooker with the stock, saffron (optional) and bay leaves.
Cook for 3 hours on LOW or 1½ hours on HIGH first, so the sausage gives its flavour to the stock.
Stir in the rinsed beans and cook for another 1–2 hours on LOW or 1 hour on HIGH. Stir gently so they stay whole.
Mash a spoonful of beans against the side of the pot for a creamy broth. Only now taste for salt: the sausage and ham (optional) are already salty.
tip: Dried fabes? Soak them for 12 hours and boil them hard on the hob for 10 minutes first; only then into the slow cooker. Beans from a jar are quicker.
kids: Spoon out the sausage separately for those who like it; dunk bread into the beans and broth.

title: Seville-Style Chickpeas with Spinach
intro: Seville's best-known tapa as a hearty stew: chickpeas and spinach in a sauce of fried bread, garlic and gentle cumin.
steps: Fry the bread and garlic cloves in olive oil until golden. Chop or pound them with the cumin, paprika and vinegar into a coarse paste: the majado.
Soften the onion in the same pan for 5 minutes. Put the onion, majado, passata, stock and chickpeas in the slow cooker and stir well.
Cook for 4–5 hours on LOW or 2–3 hours on HIGH. The bread thickens the sauce by itself into a silky stew.
Stir in the spinach in batches for the last 15 minutes; it wilts quickly. Defrost frozen spinach first and squeeze it out well.
Taste for salt and add an extra drop of vinegar if you like. Put guindilla or harissa on the table for those who like it hot.
tip: A hard-boiled egg cut into wedges turns it into a hearty meal. Choose real sherry vinegar from Jerez: it gives that typically Sevillian, gentle tang.
kids: Mash some of the chickpeas and serve as a dip with strips of bread.

title: Spanish Beef Stew with Mushrooms
intro: Beef braised gently for hours with wine, mushrooms and potatoes: a hearty estofado con setas for cool evenings.

ingredients.item: braising beef (shin or shoulder), cut into 4 cm chunks
ingredients.swap: pork shoulder (aguja) instead of beef
button mushrooms only instead of mixed mushrooms

ingredients.item: waxy potatoes, cut into large chunks

steps: Put the potatoes and carrots in the bottom of the slow cooker. Dust the meat with flour, salt and pepper and brown it all over in olive oil in batches.
Fry the mushrooms over a high heat for 5 minutes until they colour and release their liquid; that way the stew won't be watery. Set them aside.
Soften the onion and garlic for 3 minutes, deglaze with the wine (optional) and let it reduce for 3 minutes. Add the stock and scrape up the browned bits.
Lay the meat on the vegetables, pour over the juices and add the bay leaves and thyme; fill no more than three-quarters full. Cook for 8–9 hours on LOW or 5–6 hours on HIGH.
Stir in the mushrooms for the last hour. Too thin? For the last 30 minutes, stir in 1 tbsp cornflour mixed with cold water.
tip: Shin (morcillo) is full of connective tissue that turns gelatinous and tender after hours of cooking. Lean meat such as steak, on the other hand, turns dry and stringy in the slow cooker.
kids: Cut the meat and mushrooms small and give them extra potato; the gravy is mild and gentle.

title: Spanish Vegetable Stew with Fried Egg
intro: Sweet peppers, courgette and tomato slowly stewed into a soft pisto, topped with a fried egg: La Mancha on your plate.
steps: Cut all the vegetables into 1 cm dice. Soften the onion and peppers in olive oil for 8 minutes; that gives the sweet pisto flavour.
Put them in the slow cooker with the courgette, garlic, passata, sugar, salt and pepper. Don't add any water: the vegetables release plenty of liquid themselves.
Cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3 hours on HIGH, stirring once halfway through.
Too watery? For the last half hour, leave the lid ajar, on HIGH if needed, so the liquid evaporates and the pisto thickens.
Just before eating, fry an egg per person and lay it on the pisto. Break the yolk at the table and mop up with bread.
tip: Pisto is even better on day two and, without the egg, freezes perfectly. Leftovers? Use it as a pasta sauce or on toast with manchego.
kids: For fussy eaters, blend the pisto into a smooth sauce; stirred through pasta, nobody notices the vegetables.

title: Light Chicken in Saffron and Almond Sauce
intro: Chicken in a velvety saffron sauce, thickened with almonds and egg yolk: a lighter version of the Castilian festive dish.

ingredients.swap: bone-in chicken legs instead of thigh fillets

steps: Dust the chicken with flour, salt and pepper. Brown it on both sides in olive oil until golden and put it in the slow cooker.
Toast the almonds and garlic in the same pan until golden and set them aside. Soften the onion for 5 minutes and deglaze with the wine (optional).
Add the stock, saffron (optional) and bay leaf and pour this over the chicken. Cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH, until the chicken reaches 75 °C.
Grind the almonds, garlic, egg yolks and a splash of sauce into a smooth picada. Stir this into the sauce for the last half hour to thicken it.
Fish out the bay leaf, taste and scatter over the chopped egg white and parsley.
tip: Picada is the Spanish way to thicken: no cream or cornflour needed, and still a velvety sauce. A stick blender or mini chopper works perfectly.
kids: Mild, golden and creamy: with rice on the side, it's just like Grandma's chicken in sauce.

title: Brothy Spanish Rice with Squid and Prawns
intro: Soupy rice with tenderly braised squid, prawns and saffron: paella's looser sibling, and ideal for the slow cooker.

ingredients.es: anillas de calamar o sepia troceada
ingredients.swap: frozen pota (giant squid) instead of squid rings

steps: Soften the onion, pepper and garlic in olive oil for 6 minutes. Take the pan off the heat, stir in the paprika and add the passata: this is your sofrito.
Put the sofrito, squid, saffron (optional) and 500 ml stock in the slow cooker. Cook for 3–4 hours on LOW; this makes the squid beautifully tender.
Switch to HIGH. Bring the rest of the stock to the boil, pour it in with the rice and stir once. Cook for 40–50 minutes.
Lay the prawns on top for the last 10 minutes and close the lid. They are done as soon as they turn pink and opaque.
The rice should be cooked but still soupy, with some broth. Too dry? Add a splash of hot water. Serve straight away with lemon (optional).
tip: Use short-grain rice, not long-grain: it soaks up the stock nicely. Rice keeps cooking, so serve straight away and put leftovers in the fridge within an hour.
kids: Snip the squid rings into small pieces and give them extra prawns; the saffron rice is soft and mild.

title: Stuffed Aubergines with Mince and Tomato
intro: Aubergines stuffed with mince in tomato sauce, topped with melted cheese: Andalusian home cooking that even vegetable sceptics love.
steps: Halve the aubergines lengthways and hollow them out, leaving a 1 cm rim. Finely chop the flesh and sprinkle the shells with a little salt.
Fry the onion, pepper (optional), garlic and diced aubergine in olive oil for 5 minutes. Add the mince and oregano, fry until browned and crumbly and stir in half the tomato sauce.
Spoon the rest of the sauce with 100 ml water into the bottom of the slow cooker. Fill the aubergine shells with the mince and stand them side by side in the pot.
Cook for 4–5 hours on LOW or 2–3 hours on HIGH, until the aubergine is soft when you pierce it with a fork.
Optional: Sprinkle over the cheese and breadcrumbs and let them melt with the lid on for the last 15 minutes. Want it crispy? Pop them under the oven grill for a moment.
tip: Won't they fit? Cut the aubergines into three pieces and fill those. An oval 5–6 litre slow cooker works best; fill it no more than three-quarters full.
kids: If aubergine is still a step too far, scoop the filling and sauce out of the shell and serve it over rice.

title: Mild Butter Chicken
intro: Tender chicken in a velvety tomato and butter sauce with a hint of ginger: the Indian favourite that wins over even the fussiest eater.

ingredients.item: boneless chicken thighs, cut into large pieces
salt and a pinch of sugar

steps: Soften the onions in the butter for 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic, ginger and spices for 1 minute, until it smells wonderful.
Spoon the onion mixture into the slow cooker with the passata and tomato purée. Add the chicken and stir until everything is coated.
Put the lid on and cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH. Don't lift the lid in between: every peek costs an extra 15 minutes.
Only stir in the cream for the last 15 minutes, so the sauce doesn't split. Season with salt and a pinch of sugar.
tip: Chicken thighs stay much juicier than breast during long cooking. Like it hot? Put chilli flakes or sliced green chilli on the table so everyone can spice their own plate.
kids: Serve with rice and a spoonful of yoghurt on top: extra mild and lovely and creamy.

title: Hungarian Goulash with Paprika
intro: Fall-apart beef in a deep red paprika sauce with potatoes: Hungarian soul food that bubbles away gently all day.

ingredients.item: braising beef, cut into 4 cm chunks
ingredients.es: carne para guisar de ternera (aguja o morcillo)
ingredients.swap: pork shoulder (aguja) instead of beef

steps: Dust the meat with flour, salt and pepper. Brown it all over in hot oil in two batches; this gives you flavour and a nicely thickened sauce.
Put the potato chunks in the bottom of the slow cooker, where it's hottest, and spread the meat over the top.
Soften the onions and peppers in the same pan for 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and paprika for just 30 seconds: burnt paprika turns bitter.
Deglaze with the tomatoes, tomato purée and stock and scrape up the browned bits. Pour over the meat and cook for 8–9 hours on LOW or 5–6 hours on HIGH.
Taste and season with salt and pepper. Put the soured cream (optional) on the table rather than cooking it in; that way nothing splits.
tip: Use ordinary sweet pimentón, not the smoked pimentón de la Vera: it overpowers everything. Fill the slow cooker no more than two-thirds full, or the meat will cook unevenly.
kids: A generous spoonful of soured cream makes it extra mild; mash the potato into the sauce.

title: Beef Stroganoff with Mushrooms
intro: Tender beef and mushrooms in a creamy mustard and paprika sauce over tagliatelle: Russian comfort food that instantly becomes a family classic.

ingredients.item: braising beef, cut into 1 cm thick strips
ingredients.swap: pork shoulder (aguja) instead of beef
cooking cream instead of crème fraîche

steps: Dust the meat with flour, salt and pepper and brown it in hot oil in two batches. Spoon it into the slow cooker.
Fry the onion and mushrooms in the same pan for 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and paprika for 30 seconds.
Deglaze with the stock, mustard and Worcestershire sauce, scrape up the browned bits and pour everything over the meat. Cook for 7–8 hours on LOW or 4–5 hours on HIGH.
In a bowl, mix a few spoonfuls of the hot sauce into the crème fraîche and stir it into the stew for the last 15 minutes; that way it won't split.
Taste, season and serve over tagliatelle with a little chopped parsley (optional).
tip: Mushrooms release a lot of liquid, so you need very little stock: almost nothing evaporates in a slow cooker. Sauce still too thin? Let it thicken on HIGH with the lid off for the last half hour.
kids: Cut the meat small and toss everything through the pasta; creamy, soft and not spicy at all.

title: Korean Bulgogi Beef with Rice
intro: Sweet and savoury, glossy beef with soy, garlic and grated pear: the well-loved Korean flavour, mild enough for the whole family.

ingredients.swap: pork shoulder instead of beef

ingredients.es: salsa de soja baja en sal

steps: Stir the soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, vinegar, pear, garlic and ginger together in the slow cooker.
Stir in the meat and onion until everything is coated. Don't add any water: the meat and pear release enough liquid. Cook for 7–8 hours on LOW or 4–5 hours on HIGH.
Pull the meat into rough pieces in the pot using two forks.
Mix the cornflour with 3 tbsp cold water and stir it into the sauce. Let it thicken on HIGH for 15–20 minutes until the sauce is glossy.
Sprinkle with spring onion (optional) and sesame seeds (optional) and serve with rice and cucumber (optional).
tip: The grated pear makes the meat extra tender and sweet, just as in Korea. Don't add extra salt: soy sauce barely reduces in the slow cooker and stays salty enough.
kids: Spoon the glossy meat over rice with cucumber sticks: sweet, soft and not spicy.

title: Chicken Shawarma with Garlic Sauce
intro: Fragrant chicken with cumin, cinnamon and lemon, stuffed into warm pitta with fresh vegetables and garlic sauce: street food from the sofa.

serve.item: garlic sauce made with Greek yoghurt

steps: Mix the oil, lemon juice, garlic, spices, salt and pepper. Stir in the chicken; you can also do this the night before, covered, in the fridge.
Put the onion and pepper (optional) in the bottom of the slow cooker with the chicken and marinade on top. Don't add any water: the chicken and onion release their own juices.
Put the lid on and cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH, until the chicken is no longer pink inside.
Lift out the chicken and slice or shred it into strips. If you like, fry it in a hot pan for 5 minutes for crispy edges.
Toss the chicken back through the onions with a little of the cooking liquid and serve in warm pitta.
tip: Garlic sauce: stir 200 g Greek yoghurt with 1 grated garlic clove, a squeeze of lemon and salt. Fans can put harissa or sambal on the table.
kids: Let them fill their own pitta; with cucumber and yoghurt sauce it's fresh and mild.

title: Mild Jambalaya with Chicken and Chorizo
intro: A cheerful pot from Louisiana: chicken, mild chorizo, peppers and celery in tomato sauce, with the rice folded in at the end.

serve.item: Tabasco or Cajun seasoning at the table

steps: Fry the chorizo in a dry pan for 2 minutes until the red fat runs. Soften the onion, pepper and celery (optional) in that fat for 4 minutes; add the garlic briefly at the end.
Spoon everything into the slow cooker with the chicken, tomatoes, stock, paprika, thyme, salt and pepper and stir well.
Put the lid on and cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH.
During the last half hour, cook the rice according to the packet. Fold the rice into the jambalaya and leave it for 10 minutes on LOW to soak up the flavours.
Taste and season. Put the Tabasco (optional) on the table for anyone who likes it spicy.
tip: Fancy some prawns? Stir in 200 g raw peeled prawns for the last 15 minutes on HIGH; they are done as soon as they turn pink. Cool leftover rice quickly and eat it within a day.
kids: Children find the red rice with bits of sausage really festive; feel free to chop the celery very small.

title: Chinese Honey Soy Chicken with Broccoli
intro: Sticky-sweet chicken in a glossy honey, soy and garlic sauce, with broccoli on the side: better than the takeaway, and not spicy.

ingredients.es: salsa de soja baja en sal

ingredients.item: head of broccoli, cut into florets

steps: Stir the honey, soy sauce, ketchup, vinegar, garlic, ginger and sesame oil (optional) together in the slow cooker.
Add the chicken and turn to coat. Don't add any water. Cook for 4–5 hours on LOW or 2½–3 hours on HIGH.
Lift out the chicken and cut it into pieces. Mix the cornflour with 3 tbsp cold water and stir it into the sauce.
Switch to HIGH, add the broccoli and cook with the lid on for 20–30 minutes, until the sauce thickens and the broccoli is just tender.
Toss the chicken back through the sauce and sprinkle with spring onion (optional) and sesame seeds (optional).
tip: Choose low-salt soy sauce: almost nothing reduces in the slow cooker, so the salt stays concentrated. Fans of heat can put sriracha or chilli oil on the table separately.
kids: Sweet, sticky and fun to try with chopsticks; the broccoli florets become 'little trees' in the sauce.

title: Caribbean Chicken with Sweet Potato and Pineapple
intro: Sunny chicken with allspice, thyme and lime, with sweet potato, pineapple and beans: a mild taste of the Caribbean at your table.

ingredients.item: sweet potato, cut into 3 cm chunks

ingredients.es: pimienta de Jamaica molida (Carrefour of Marokkaanse winkel)

steps: Put the sweet potato, onion and pepper (optional) in the bottom of the slow cooker: vegetables cook more slowly than meat, so they belong at the bottom.
Rub the chicken with the garlic, ginger, allspice, thyme, salt and pepper and lay it on the vegetables.
Pour over the pineapple and its juice and put the lid on. Cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH.
Optional: Stir in the beans for the last half hour; they only need to warm through.
Pull the chicken into rough pieces, stir in the lime zest and juice and taste for salt once more.
tip: Use tinned or jarred beans: raw dried kidney beans don't get hot enough in a slow cooker to break down their natural toxin. Put hot pepper sauce on the table separately.
kids: Sweet potato and pineapple make this naturally sweet; mash it up for the littlest ones.

title: Sticky BBQ Spare Ribs
intro: Spare ribs that slide off the bone, with a sticky coating of barbecue sauce from the oven: an American feast for the whole family.
steps: Mix both paprikas, the sugar, garlic powder and salt and rub it all over the ribs. Cut them into sections of 3–4 ribs.
Put the onion in the bottom and stand the ribs upright around the sides, meaty side facing out. That way they cook evenly.
Mix the barbecue sauce, ketchup, honey (optional) and vinegar and pour half over the ribs. Don't add any water. Cook for 7–8 hours on LOW or 4–5 hours on HIGH.
Preheat the oven grill to 220 °C. Carefully lay the ribs on a baking tray lined with baking paper; cooked meat falls off the bone easily.
Brush with the rest of the sauce and grill for 8–10 minutes, until glossy and sticky.
tip: Skim the fat off the cooking liquid and boil the liquid down in a saucepan into a thick dipping sauce. Pull leftover meat off the bone: tomorrow's tasty sandwich.
kids: Eating ribs with your hands is a treat; give them a little pot of sauce for dipping and plenty of napkins.

title: Japanese Pork Curry
intro: Thick, sweetish Japanese curry with tender pork, carrots and potatoes: in Japan it's children's all-time favourite, and it's easy to see why.

ingredients.item: pork shoulder, cut into 3 cm chunks
ingredients.es: carne de cerdo para guisar (paleta o aguja)

ingredients.item: carrots, cut into chunks on the diagonal

ingredients.es: Golden Curry o Vermont Curry mild (tienda asiática)
ingredients.swap: curry powder with flour instead of curry roux blocks

steps: Brown the meat all over in hot oil in two batches; this gives the sauce a deeper flavour.
Put the carrots and potatoes in the bottom of the slow cooker, then the meat, onion and grated apple (optional). Pour over the stock, soy sauce and honey (optional).
Put the lid on and cook for 7–8 hours on LOW or 4–5 hours on HIGH, until the meat and carrots are tender.
Break the curry blocks into pieces and stir them into the cooking liquid. Let it thicken on HIGH for 20–30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Only taste once it has thickened: the blocks are already salty, so extra salt is usually unnecessary.
tip: No Asian shop nearby? Cook 3 tbsp flour with 2 tbsp butter and 2 tbsp mild curry powder for 2 minutes into a roux and stir it in at the end.
kids: Japanese children eat this every week: just mash the soft vegetables into the rice.

title: Dutch Hachee with Red Cabbage
intro: Classic Dutch hachee: beef in a sweet-and-sour onion gravy with bay leaves and cloves. With red cabbage and mash, it's a real treat.

ingredients.item: braising beef (chuck or silverside), cut into 3 cm chunks
ingredients.es: carne para guisar (aguja o morcillo de ternera)
ingredients.swap: pork shoulder (aguja) instead of beef

ingredients.item: apple sauce + 1 tbsp honey (instead of Dutch apple syrup)
speculoos biscuits (instead of Dutch spiced cake)

serve.item: jarred red cabbage, warmed with an apple (lombarda en conserva)

steps: Dust the meat with flour, salt and pepper and brown it in butter in two batches. Put it in the slow cooker.
Cook the onions in the same pan for 8 minutes until soft and golden. Deglaze with the stock and vinegar and scrape up the browned bits.
Pour the onions over the meat. Add the bay leaves, cloves, apple sauce and honey and crumble the biscuits over the top.
Put the lid on and cook for 8–9 hours on LOW or 5–6 hours on HIGH. Don't open it in between: every peek costs heat and time.
Fish out the bay leaves and cloves. Stir the meat until it falls into shreds and taste: add a little extra vinegar or honey for the sweet-and-sour balance.
tip: Dutch spiced cake (ontbijtkoek) is hard to find in Spain; Lotus biscuits thicken and spice the gravy just as well. Too thin? Let the hachee thicken on HIGH with the lid off for half an hour.
kids: Shredded beef with mash and a little well of gravy: soft and sweetish. Fish out the onion rings for fussy eaters.

title: Old-Fashioned Dutch Pea Soup with Smoked Sausage
intro: Thick Dutch snert with split peas, vegetables and sausage. Just right for that rare cold winter's day on the Costa.

ingredients.item: pork ribs or pork belly slices
ingredients.es: costillas de cerdo o panceta fresca

ingredients.item: celeriac, or 3 sticks of celery, diced
Dutch smoked sausage or 4 smoked sausages
ingredients.swap: Spanish smoked sausages instead of Dutch smoked sausage

steps: Rinse the split peas in a sieve until the water runs clear; no need to soak them. Put them in the slow cooker with the water, stock cubes and bay leaf.
Chop the leek, celery, carrots, onion and potato small and stir them in. Lay the ribs or pork belly on top.
Cook for 8–9 hours on LOW or 4–5 hours on HIGH. Stir once after a few hours, as split peas sink to the bottom.
Lift out the meat, pull it off the bones and chop it small. Return the meat and the sliced sausage and heat for another half hour.
Stir the soup vigorously or blend part of it. Too thick? Add hot water. Only now season with salt and pepper.
tip: Split peas can be tricky to find: try Carrefour, Lidl theme weeks or an international shop. Snert gets even thicker after a night in the fridge; thin it with water when reheating.
kids: Ladle out a small bowl of soup with slices of sausage and give them a piece of toast for dipping.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon with or without Wine
intro: The French classic stew with tender beef, bacon, mushrooms and baby onions. With red wine or mosto tinto: both rich and mild.

ingredients.item: braising beef, cut into 4 cm chunks
ingredients.swap: pork shoulder (aguja) instead of beef

ingredients.item: red wine, or mosto tinto + 1 tbsp red wine vinegar
bay leaves and a sprig of thyme

steps: Fry the lardons in a frying pan until the fat runs and spoon them into the slow cooker. Dust the meat with flour, salt and pepper and brown it in batches.
Briefly fry the onions, carrot and garlic in the same fat, stir in the tomato purée and spoon everything in with the meat.
Pour the wine into the pan and let it boil hard for 5 minutes: alcohol barely evaporates in a closed slow cooker. Mosto tinto only needs warming.
Add the stock, bay leaves and thyme, scrape up the browned bits and pour everything over the meat. Cook for 8–9 hours on LOW or 5–6 hours on HIGH.
Fry the mushrooms (optional) until golden and stir them in for the last hour. Fish out the bay leaves and taste for salt and pepper.
tip: Alcohol-free: use mosto tinto (red grape juice, in every Spanish supermarket) with a tablespoon of vinegar to balance the sweetness. No shallots? Halve ordinary small onions.
kids: If you cook with wine, some alcohol always remains; mosto tinto is the safe version for children.

title: French Mustard Chicken with Tarragon
intro: Poulet à la moutarde, family style: juicy chicken thighs in a creamy, mild mustard sauce with tarragon. Weeknight French, without the fuss.
steps: Dust the chicken with flour, salt and pepper and brown it for 2–3 minutes on each side until golden. Put the chicken in the slow cooker.
Soften the onion, garlic and carrot in the same pan for 3 minutes. Deglaze with the stock, stir in the mustard and pour this over the chicken.
Scatter over the mushrooms (optional) and tarragon. Cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3 hours on HIGH, until the chicken is cooked through and tender.
Stir in the cooking cream and let it thicken for another half hour on HIGH with the lid off. Cream goes in only now: long cooking makes dairy split.
Taste and season with salt, pepper or an extra spoonful of mustard. Sprinkle with fresh parsley if you like.
tip: Chicken thighs stay juicy in the slow cooker, while breast dries out more quickly. Always use defrosted chicken: frozen meat stays lukewarm for too long, and that lets bacteria grow.
kids: Mustard turns mild and sweetish as it cooks. Cut the chicken into strips and spoon the sauce over rice.

title: Liège Meatballs in Syrup Sauce
intro: Belgian boulets à la liégeoise: juicy meatballs in a sweet-and-sour onion sauce. With chips or baguette, big and little eaters alike tuck in.

ingredients.item: honey + 2 tbsp apple sauce (instead of Liège syrup)

steps: Mix the mince, egg, breadcrumbs, nutmeg, salt and pepper and roll into 8–10 large balls. Brown them all over in butter; that way they hold together.
Put the meatballs in the slow cooker. Cook the onions in the same fat for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Deglaze with the stock and stir in the honey, apple sauce, vinegar and sugar. Pour over the meatballs and add the bay leaves and cloves.
Cook for 6–7 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH. The mince must be cooked right through, with no pink centre.
Fish out the bay leaves and cloves. Thicken the sauce with cornflour mixed with cold water and let it cook for another 15 minutes on HIGH.
tip: Liège syrup is rarely found here. Honey with apple sauce comes surprisingly close; if you have Dutch apple syrup (appelstroop), use that. Roll the balls with wet hands so nothing sticks.
kids: Halve a meatball, dip the chips in the sweet sauce and that's it: that Belgian chip-shop feeling without a deep-fat fryer.

title: British Sausage Casserole with White Beans
intro: British sausage casserole: browned sausages, white beans and vegetables in a mild tomato sauce. Cheap, filling and loved by children.

ingredients.es: caldo de pollo o de verduras

steps: Brown the sausages all over in oil for 8 minutes; they don't need to be cooked through yet. Then cut them in half.
Cut the onion, carrots and pepper (optional) into pieces, put them in the bottom of the slow cooker and lay the sausages on top.
Mix the garlic, chopped tomatoes, stock, paprika and Worcestershire sauce (optional) and pour over the sausages.
Cook for 6–7 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH. Stir in the drained beans for the last hour so they stay whole.
Taste and season with pepper and salt if needed. Mash a few beans against the side of the pot for a thicker sauce.
tip: Use jarred or tinned beans. Dried red kidney beans must first be boiled hard for 10 minutes: the slow cooker doesn't get hot enough to break down their toxin.
kids: Cut the sausages into coins and serve with mash: a homemade, less sugary version of baked beans.

title: Minestrone with White Beans and Soup Pasta
intro: Italian vegetable soup packed with beans, vegetables and little pasta shapes. A complete, budget-friendly meal and a clever way to empty the vegetable drawer.

serve.item: grated hard cheese (vegetarian: made without animal rennet)

steps: Cut the onion, carrots, celery, courgette (optional) and potato into 1 cm dice. Small, even pieces cook evenly and fit on a child's spoon.
Put the vegetables, garlic, chopped tomatoes, stock and herbs in the slow cooker and stir. Fill the pot no more than three-quarters full.
Cook for 6–7 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH, until the carrot is tender.
Switch to HIGH, stir in the pasta and drained beans and cook with the lid on for another 25–30 minutes. Pasta always goes in at the end.
Become too thick? Add a splash of hot water. Taste for salt and pepper and serve with grated cheese.
tip: Freezing? Do it without the pasta: it soaks up the soup and goes soft. When reheating, simply cook a handful of fresh pasta in it.
kids: Choose star or alphabet pasta and let them sprinkle their own cheese: the vegetables will vanish all by themselves.

title: Stuffed Peppers with Mince and Rice
intro: Hungarian töltött paprika, kept mild: peppers stuffed with mince and rice, slowly cooked in tomato sauce. A complete meal on one plate.

ingredients.item: beef mince or mixed beef and pork mince
ingredients.swap: pork mince instead of beef mince

steps: Cut the tops off the peppers and remove the seeds. Trim the bottoms straight if needed, so they stand steady.
Mix the mince, rice, onion, egg, paprika, salt and pepper and loosely fill the peppers.
Stir the passata, water, sugar and oregano together in the slow cooker. Stand the peppers upright in the sauce and put their tops back on.
Cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3 hours on HIGH. The filling is cooked when it's no longer pink inside (75 °C).
Sprinkle over the cheese (optional) and let it melt with the lid on for another 10–15 minutes. Spoon sauce over the peppers when serving.
tip: Use pre-cooked rice: raw rice stays hard in a firm mince filling. Yesterday's leftovers or a vasito de arroz cocido from the supermarket is perfect.
kids: Not sure about peppers? Give them just the filling with sauce first; they can try the pepper later.

title: Turkey Fricassée with Mushrooms and Peas
intro: Dutch-style fricassée with turkey in a light, creamy sauce with mushrooms and peas. Gentle in flavour, so very child-friendly.

ingredients.item: turkey thigh or breast, cut into 3 cm chunks
ingredients.es: muslo de pavo deshuesado o pechuga de pavo

steps: Season the turkey with salt and pepper and sear it briefly in butter, just for colour. Spoon it into the slow cooker.
Add the onion, carrot, mushrooms, stock and bay leaf. Cook for 4–5 hours on LOW or 2½–3 hours on HIGH; lean turkey dries out if cooked for longer.
Switch to HIGH. Stir the cornflour into the cooking cream until smooth and stir this into the stew along with the peas (optional).
Let it cook for another 20 minutes until the sauce thickens and the peas (optional) are hot. Fish out the bay leaf.
Season with lemon juice, nutmeg, salt and pepper. A squeeze of lemon makes the creamy sauce fresher.
tip: Turkey thigh (muslo de pavo) stays juicier than breast and is often cheaper; with breast, stick to the shortest time. Frozen peas can go in straight from the freezer, as the stew is already hot by then.
kids: Rice with white sauce, peas and soft pieces of turkey: the mild plateful almost every child loves.

title: Chicken Pasta Bake with Broccoli and Cheese
intro: All the flavour of a pasta bake without the oven: chicken in a creamy tomato sauce with pasta and broccoli, finished with melted cheese. One pot, everyone happy.
steps: Put the chicken, onion, garlic, passata, stock, herbs, salt and pepper in the slow cooker and stir well.
Cook for 4–5 hours on LOW or 2½–3 hours on HIGH, until the chicken is cooked through and tender.
Switch to HIGH. Stir in the uncooked pasta, hot water and broccoli; make sure the pasta is covered by the sauce.
Cook with the lid on for 25–35 minutes until the pasta is al dente. Stir once after 15 minutes so nothing sticks to the bottom.
Optional: Stir in the cooking cream, sprinkle over the cheese and let it melt with the lid on for 10 minutes. Serve straight away.
tip: Pasta quickly goes too soft in the slow cooker: set a timer from 25 minutes and taste. Wholewheat pasta needs a little longer and stays firmer.
kids: Let the children sprinkle the cheese themselves; the little broccoli trees among the pasta will barely be noticed.

title: Lentil Dal with Spinach and Coconut
intro: Creamy red lentils with a gentle curry flavour, coconut milk and fresh spinach: comforting, nourishing and dirt cheap.
steps: Soften the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil for 3 minutes. Stir in the curry powder and cumin and fry for 1 minute; this brings the spices to life.
Rinse the lentils in a sieve until the water runs clear. Put them in the slow cooker with the onion mixture, tomatoes and stock and stir well.
Put the lid on and cook for 6–7 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH, until the lentils are completely soft and creamy.
Optional: Stir in the coconut milk and lay the spinach on top. Let it wilt with the lid on for 10 minutes, then stir everything together.
Season with salt and pepper. Too thick? Thin with a splash of hot water; the dal thickens a little more as it stands.
tip: Red lentils don't need soaking: they collapse by themselves into a creamy purée. A squeeze of lemon just before serving makes the dal fresh and lively.
kids: Serve with rice and a spoonful of yoghurt stirred in: lovely and creamy and extra mild.

title: Sweet Potato Chilli sin Carne
intro: Beans, sweetcorn and sweet potato in a mild, smoky tomato sauce: a chilli where nobody misses the meat.

ingredients.item: sweet potato, cut into 2 cm dice

steps: Soften the onion and peppers in the oil for 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic, paprika and cumin and fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Put the sweet potato in the bottom of the slow cooker. Spoon the onion mixture on top and add the beans, sweetcorn (optional), tomatoes and stock. Stir.
Put the lid on and cook for 6–7 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH, until the sweet potato is tender.
Mash a few spoonfuls of beans and potato against the side of the pot for a thicker chilli. Season with salt and pepper.
tip: Always use jarred or tinned beans: raw dried kidney beans don't get hot enough in the slow cooker to break down their toxin. Anyone who wants heat can add their own chilli flakes.
kids: Let them fill their own tortilla with chilli, cheese and a spoonful of soured cream.

title: Ratatouille with Chickpeas
intro: Summery Provençal vegetables that slowly melt together, with chickpeas for a hearty, protein-rich one-pot meal.
steps: Fry the aubergine in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes until golden; this adds flavour and prevents grey, floppy pieces.
Soften the onion and garlic in the rest of the oil. Put everything in the slow cooker with the courgette, peppers, chickpeas, tomatoes, purée, herbs and sugar.
Don't add any extra liquid: the vegetables release plenty of juice themselves. Put the lid on and cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH.
Sauce too thin? Leave the lid ajar for the last half hour. Season with salt and pepper.
tip: Cut the courgette into bigger chunks than the aubergine so it doesn't fall apart. Also lovely the next day, lukewarm with a fried egg on top.
kids: Spoon it over couscous and sprinkle with cheese; the chickpeas are often the favourite.

title: Slow Cooker Aubergine and Courgette Lasagne
intro: Layers of aubergine, pasta, creamy ricotta and tomato sauce with melted mozzarella: lasagne without an oven, and still wonderfully oozy.
steps: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the courgette, tomatoes, purée and oregano and let it bubble for 5 minutes. Don't add any water.
Grease the inner pot. Lay half the aubergine slices on the bottom and cover with lasagne sheets, broken where needed.
Spoon over a third of the sauce with dollops of ricotta. Repeat the aubergine, sheets and ricotta and finish with the rest of the sauce.
Make sure all the sheets are covered by sauce. Cook for 2½–3 hours on HIGH or 4–4½ hours on LOW, until the pasta and aubergine are tender.
Switch off, scatter over the mozzarella (optional) and let it melt and set for 10 minutes with the lid on.
tip: Don't let the lasagne cook any longer than needed, as pasta quickly goes mushy in the slow cooker. Dry edges? Those sheets weren't covered by sauce: press them down well next time.
kids: Give them a corner piece with a crispy cheesy edge; that's the best bit.

title: Creamy Pumpkin and Carrot Soup
intro: Velvety orange soup of pumpkin, carrot and a hint of apple: sweetish, mild and a hit with children.
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until translucent. Cut the pumpkin, carrot, potato and apple (optional) into even pieces of about 3 cm.
Put everything in the slow cooker with the garlic, nutmeg and stock; the stock only needs to just cover the vegetables.
Put the lid on and cook for 6–7 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH, until the pumpkin is completely soft.
Blend until smooth with a stick blender. Only now stir in the cream (optional) and warm through for 10 minutes without letting it boil, so it doesn't split.
Season with salt and pepper. Too thick? Thin it with a splash of hot stock.
tip: Ready-cut calabaza in tubs saves on peeling. Freezing? Do it before adding the cream, and only stir the cream in after reheating.
kids: Use a teaspoon of cream to draw a spider's web or a smiley face on the soup: instant party.

title: Mussels and Prawns in Tomato and Pepper Sauce
intro: A gentle Spanish tomato sauce that simmers for hours, with mussels and prawns that only go in at the very end.
steps: Soften the onion, pepper and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes. Put them in the slow cooker with the tomatoes, paprika and stock.
Cook the sauce for 4–5 hours on LOW or 2–3 hours on HIGH. Meanwhile, rinse the mussels; throw away any that are broken, or open ones that don't close when tapped.
Switch the slow cooker to HIGH. Stir the mussels and prawns (optional) into the hot sauce, put the lid on and cook for 20–30 minutes.
Stir once halfway through. The prawns (optional) are done when they are pink and firm; by then the mussels will have opened.
Throw away any mussels that stay closed. Season, sprinkle with parsley (optional) and squeeze over the lemon (optional).
tip: Shellfish only goes in at the end: they cook in half an hour, but after hours they turn as tough as rubber bands. Defrost frozen prawns overnight in the fridge first.
kids: Use an empty mussel shell as a little pincer and dip the bread in the sauce.

title: Hake on a Bed of Vegetables with Lemon
intro: Soft potatoes, peppers and courgette cook for hours; the hake steams on top at the end until it flakes perfectly.

ingredients.item: waxy potatoes, cut into 1 cm slices

ingredients.swap: frozen coley instead of hake

serve.item: mayonnaise with a squeeze of lemon

steps: Lay the potato slices in the bottom of the slow cooker, where it's hottest. Spoon the onion, pepper, courgette (optional), tomato and garlic on top.
Pour over the stock and oil and season with salt and pepper. Cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH, until the potato is tender.
Switch to HIGH. Season the hake with salt, pepper and lemon zest and lay the fillets on the vegetables, with a few lemon slices on top.
Put the lid on and cook for 30–45 minutes, until the fish is white and opaque and flakes easily.
Carefully lift out the fish with a spatula and serve on the vegetables with parsley (optional) and a drizzle of olive oil.
tip: Defrost frozen hake overnight in the fridge and pat it dry: frozen fish cools the pot down and stays lukewarm for too long. Thick fillets need a little longer.
kids: Check quickly for small bones and mash the fish with potato and a little of the juices.

title: Rice Pudding with Lemon and Cinnamon
intro: Spanish rice pudding just like Grandma made it: creamy, with lemon peel and cinnamon, without hours of stirring at the hob.

ingredients.item: lemon (peel only, without the white pith)

steps: Grease the inner pot halfway up the sides with butter; this stops it sticking. Heat the milk in a pan until almost boiling.
Don't rinse the rice: the starch makes the pudding creamy. Put the rice, hot milk, sugar, lemon peel, cinnamon stick and salt in the slow cooker.
Cook for 2½–3 hours on HIGH or 4–5 hours on LOW. Give it a stir every hour, especially at the start, so the rice doesn't stick to the bottom.
The pudding is ready when the rice is soft and still loose; it thickens considerably as it cools. Fish out the peel and cinnamon stick.
Serve warm or cold, sprinkled with ground cinnamon (optional).
tip: Become too thick? Stir in a splash of warm milk. Cold from the fridge is actually the classic way to eat arroz con leche in Spain; keep it covered for up to 3 days.
kids: Let them use a paper stencil to sprinkle a cinnamon heart or their own initial on their bowl.

title: Pears Poached in Grape Juice with Cinnamon
intro: Whole pears that slowly turn deep red in spiced grape juice: a festive alcohol-free pudding for the whole family.
steps: Peel the pears, leaving the stalk on. Slice the bottoms flat so they can stand and scoop out the core from underneath with a teaspoon.
Stand the pears upright in the slow cooker. Pour in the grape juice with the honey (optional), cinnamon, cloves, orange peel (optional) and vanilla (optional).
Cook for 4–5 hours on LOW or 2–3 hours on HIGH, until a small knife slides in easily. Turn them over in the juice once halfway through.
Lift out the pears. Boil the juice in a small pan with the cornflour mixture for 2 minutes into a glossy syrup.
Serve the pears warm or cold with the syrup and a spoonful of yoghurt or ice cream.
tip: Choose firm pears that aren't quite ripe: soft pears fall apart. Fish out the cloves before serving, as biting on one is no fun.
kids: Slice the pear into little fans and add a scoop of vanilla ice cream; the syrup is the sauce.

title: Warm Slow Cooker Chocolate Brownie
intro: A fudgy brownie with crisp edges, baked in the slow cooker while you get on with something else. Lovely served warm with ice cream.

ingredients.es: papel de horno y papel de cocina
