steps: Line the inner pot with baking paper that hangs over the edge; that way you can lift the brownie out in one go later.
Melt the butter and chocolate together over a low heat. Off the heat, whisk in the sugar, eggs and vanilla (optional) until glossy.
Briefly fold in the flour, cocoa and salt, just until there's no flour visible. Smooth the batter out in the pot.
Lay two layers of kitchen paper over the opening to catch dripping condensation and put the lid on. Cook for 2–2½ hours on HIGH or 3–3½ hours on LOW.
It's ready when the edges are firm and a skewer from the centre comes out with moist crumbs. Leave to set for 30 minutes with the lid off.
tip: Don't let the kitchen paper hang over the hot outside of the pot, and replace it if it gets soaked. Like it extra fudgy? Take the brownie out 15 minutes earlier.
kids: Let them help stir and then top their own brownie with strawberries or a scoop of ice cream.

title: Pork in Tomato Sauce
intro: Tender pork in a sweet, thick tomato sauce: the quintessential Andalusian home-cooked dish, which every abuela makes her own way.

ingredients.item: pork shoulder, cut into 3 cm chunks

steps: Dust the meat with flour, salt and pepper and brown it all over in olive oil in batches. Put it in the slow cooker.
Soften the onion, pepper and garlic in the same pan for 5 minutes. Deglaze with the wine (optional) and let it reduce for 2 minutes.
Stir in the passata, sugar, oregano and bay leaves and pour this over the meat; fill no more than three-quarters full. Cook for 7–8 hours on LOW or 4–5 hours on HIGH.
Sauce too thin? Leave the lid ajar for the last half hour. Fish out the bay leaves and taste for salt and pepper.
Serve with chips or bread. Put guindilla or pimentón picante on the table for anyone who wants some heat.
tip: Ask the butcher for 'magro' or 'aguja': shoulder meat with a little fat stays juicy. Tenderloin or loin, on the other hand, turns dry in the slow cooker.
kids: Chips on the side and a sweet tomato sauce for dipping: guaranteed clean plates.

title: Aragonese Chicken with Peppers and Serrano Ham
intro: Chicken braised with sweet peppers, tomato and a hint of serrano ham: a colourful classic from Aragón that is naturally mild.
steps: Season the chicken with salt and pepper and brown it on both sides in olive oil until golden. Put it in the slow cooker.
Fry the ham (optional) in the same pan for 2 minutes. Add the onion, peppers and garlic and soften for 6 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the paprika, deglaze with the wine (optional), let it reduce for 2 minutes and add the passata.
Pour this over the chicken and add the bay leaf. Cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH, until the chicken reaches 75 °C.
Fish out the bay leaf and taste carefully for salt: the ham is already salty. Sprinkle with parsley.
tip: Chilindrón is all about sweet peppers. Want an extra-deep flavour? Stir in 1 tbsp ñora paste (carne de pimiento choricero); it's smoky but not hot.
kids: Shred the chicken and mix it with rice and the sweet pepper sauce.

title: Córdoba-Style Oxtail Stew
intro: Oxtail braised all day in red wine until the meat slides off the bone: Córdoba's proudest slow-simmered dish.

ingredients.swap: 1 kg pork cheeks instead of oxtail

steps: Dust the oxtail with flour, salt and pepper and brown it all over until deep brown in olive oil, in batches; take your time, this is where the flavour comes from.
Soften the onion, carrot, leek (optional), pepper and garlic in the same pan for 6 minutes. Pour in the wine (optional) and let it bubble hard for 4 minutes.
Add the stock and herbs and pour everything over the meat; fill no more than three-quarters full. Cook for 9–10 hours on LOW or 6–7 hours on HIGH.
The meat should fall off the bone. Lift it out and spoon the fat off the juices, or let the stew set overnight in the fridge.
Fish out the herbs, blend the vegetables and juices into a glossy sauce, pick the meat off the bones and return it to the pot.
tip: Rabo de toro is at its best on day two: put it in the fridge overnight, lift off the solidified fat and reheat it on the hob.
kids: Pick the meat off the bones and serve it with chips and a spoonful of sauce.

title: Basque Tuna and Potato Stew
intro: The fishermen's stew from the Basque Country: potatoes and peppers simmered for hours, with juicy tuna that only goes in at the very end.

ingredients.item: fresh tuna or bonito, cut into 3 cm chunks
ingredients.es: atún fresco o bonito del norte
ingredients.swap: fresh mackerel (verdel) instead of tuna

steps: Soften the onion, peppers and garlic in olive oil for 6 minutes. Stir in the ñora paste or paprika and the passata: this is your sofrito.
Peel the potatoes, nick them with a knife and break them into pieces: the released starch thickens the broth. Put them in the bottom of the slow cooker.
Spoon the sofrito, stock and bay leaf over the top. Cook for 6–7 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH, until the potato is tender.
Switch to HIGH, season the tuna with salt and lay it on top. Put the lid on and cook for 10–15 minutes; any longer and tuna turns dry.
Fish out the bay leaf, stir very gently and sprinkle with parsley.
tip: Defrost frozen tuna in the fridge. Budget version: stir two tins of tuna in olive oil through it at the table, just as tasty and child-proof.
kids: Mash the tuna and potato with a little broth into a mild fish stew.

title: Valencian Orange Chicken with Honey
intro: Chicken in a glossy sauce of freshly squeezed orange and honey: sunny, sweet and sour and just right for children.

ingredients.item: freshly squeezed orange juice (3–4 oranges) plus the zest of 1

steps: Dust the chicken with flour, salt and pepper and brown it on both sides in olive oil until golden. Put it in the slow cooker.
Soften the onion, garlic and carrot for 4 minutes. Stir in the paprika and deglaze with the juice, stock, honey (optional) and zest.
Pour this over the chicken. Cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH, until the chicken reaches 75 °C.
Mix the cornflour with 2 tbsp cold water and stir it into the sauce for the last 30 minutes; switch to HIGH and keep the lid on.
Taste: too sweet? A splash of lemon juice restores the balance. Sprinkle with parsley.
tip: Juicing oranges ('naranjas de zumo') are dirt cheap in winter. Only grate the orange part of the peel; the white pith makes the sauce bitter.
kids: Sweet and sour and glossy, just like the takeaway: with rice, it's an instant favourite.

title: Andalusian Chickpea Pot with Chicken
intro: A clear broth with vermicelli to start, followed by chicken, vegetables and chickpeas: the Andalusian Sunday pot that warms the whole family.

ingredients.item: ham bone or 150 g serrano ham in one piece
ingredients.es: hueso de jamón o taco de jamón

steps: Put the potato, carrot, leek and celery in the bottom of the slow cooker. Lay the chicken and ham on top and add the bay leaf.
Pour in water until everything is just covered; fill no more than three-quarters full. Cook for 7–8 hours on LOW or 4–5 hours on HIGH, until the chicken reaches 75 °C.
Stir in the chickpeas for the last hour and skim any fat and scum off the broth if needed.
Ladle 1 litre of broth into a pan, bring to the boil and cook the vermicelli for 3–4 minutes until tender. Taste for salt.
Serve the soup first with a mint leaf (optional), then the chicken, vegetables and chickpeas with a drizzle of olive oil.
tip: Pick the meat off the bones and mash it together with a few vegetables: that's the 'pringá', delicious on bread. Leftover broth is liquid gold for rice.
kids: Vermicelli soup with tender chicken: the Spanish chicken noodle soup they'll recognise straight away.

title: Cuttlefish with Peas and Potatoes
intro: Cuttlefish slowly braised until butter-soft with tomato, white wine and sweet peas: an Andalusian coastal classic for the slow cooker.

ingredients.item: cleaned cuttlefish, cut into pieces (frozen, defrosted)
ingredients.swap: frozen pota (squid) instead of cuttlefish

steps: Put the diced potato in the bottom of the slow cooker. Pat the cuttlefish dry, fry it in hot olive oil for 3 minutes and spoon it over the potato.
Soften the onion and garlic in the same pan for 5 minutes. Deglaze with the wine (optional), let it reduce for 2 minutes and add the passata and stock.
Pour this over the cuttlefish and add the bay leaf. Cook for 4–5 hours on LOW or 2–3 hours on HIGH, until a fork slides in easily.
Stir in the peas for the last half hour; they can go in frozen. Put the lid straight back on.
Fish out the bay leaf, taste for salt and pepper and sprinkle with parsley.
tip: Cuttlefish turns tough at first and then butter-soft after long braising: ideal for the slow cooker. Frozen cuttlefish from the supermarket is already cleaned and ready to use.
kids: Cut the cuttlefish small; with peas and potato, it's a mild fish stew.

title: Stuffed Peppers with Rice, Vegetables and Cheese
intro: Sweet red peppers stuffed with rice, courgette, mushrooms and manchego, braised in tomato sauce: colourful, filling and completely vegetarian.

ingredients.swap: ordinary grated cheese instead of manchego

steps: Cut the tops off the peppers and remove the seeds. Soften the onion, garlic, courgette and mushrooms (optional) in olive oil for 6 minutes until the liquid has evaporated.
Mix the vegetables with the rice, half the passata, the oregano, egg, half the cheese, salt and pepper. Fill the peppers.
Spoon the rest of the passata with 100 ml water into the bottom. Stand the peppers upright in it and put their tops back on.
Cook for 4–5 hours on LOW or 2½–3 hours on HIGH, until the peppers are soft.
Sprinkle the rest of the cheese over the top for the last 15 minutes and let it melt with the lid on. Serve with the sauce.
tip: Use pre-cooked rice: raw rice cooks unevenly in a filling. Pepper leaning over? Slice a thin sliver off the bottom.
kids: Let them fill their own pepper and put the 'little lid' on top; then they'll eat it too.

title: Bread Pudding with Orange and Raisins
intro: Yesterday's bread becomes a golden, creamy pudding with orange, cinnamon and raisins: a comforting British pud and the tastiest way to waste nothing.

ingredients.item: day-old bread (baguette or white bread), sliced

steps: Grease the inside of the slow cooker generously with butter. Spread the bread slices thinly with the soft butter and cut them in half.
Layer the bread in the slow cooker, overlapping like roof tiles, and scatter the raisins (optional) and orange zest between the layers.
Whisk together the eggs, milk, cream (optional), sugar, vanilla, cinnamon and salt. Pour this over the bread, press it down with a spoon and leave to soak for 15 minutes.
Lay two layers of kitchen paper over the opening and put the lid on. Cook for 3–3½ hours on LOW or 1½–2 hours on HIGH, until the pudding has set in the middle: a knife will then come out clean.
Remove the lid and let the pudding firm up for 10 minutes. Sprinkle with brown sugar (optional) and serve warm or lukewarm, with custard if you like.
tip: The drier the bread, the better it soaks up the egg and milk without turning soggy: perfect for yesterday's leftover barra. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and eat them within 2 days; a quick blast in the microwave makes them soft and creamy again.
kids: Let them butter the bread and scatter the raisins. Anyone who doesn't like raisins simply gets a corner without.

title: Greek Stifado with Shallots and Orzo
intro: Beef with sweet shallots in tomato, red wine and a hint of cinnamon: Greek winter food that goes beautifully with orzo.

ingredients.item: braising beef (shoulder or shin), cut into chunks
ingredients.swap: pork shoulder instead of beef
ordinary onions, cut into wedges, instead of shallots

steps: Dust the meat with flour, salt and pepper and brown it all over in olive oil in batches. Put it in the slow cooker.
Fry the shallots for 5 minutes until golden, then add the garlic and tomato purée for 1 minute. Deglaze with the wine (optional) and let it reduce for 3 minutes.
Add the passata, vinegar, cinnamon, cloves and bay leaves and pour this over the meat. Cook for 8–9 hours on LOW or 5–6 hours on HIGH.
Fish out the cinnamon, cloves and bay leaves. Too thin? Leave the lid ajar for the last half hour.
Cook the orzo according to the packet and spoon the stifado over the top.
tip: Peeling shallots is quick if you put them in boiling water for 2 minutes: the skins slip right off. A little feta on top makes it completely Greek.
kids: The cinnamon makes the sauce gentle and a touch sweet; orzo slips down just like rice.

title: Sweet and Sour Tofu with Peppers and Pineapple
intro: Crispy tofu, peppers and pineapple in a glossy sweet and sour sauce, just like from the Chinese takeaway: completely plant-based, mild and ready with a pan of rice.

ingredients.item: pineapple chunks in juice, drained (keep the juice)

ingredients.es: salsa de soja baja en sal

ingredients.item: peppers (red and yellow), in 3 cm pieces

steps: Stir the pineapple juice, ketchup, vinegar, sugar, soy sauce, garlic and ginger together in the slow cooker. Keep the pineapple chunks covered in the fridge.
Add the onion, pepper and carrot (optional) and toss. Don't add any water: the vegetables release their own liquid. Cook for 3–4 hours on LOW or 1½–2 hours on HIGH, until the vegetables are soft.

Drain the tofu, pat it very dry with kitchen paper and cut it into 2 cm cubes. Toss the cubes in 2 tbsp cornflour and fry them in the oil for 8–10 minutes until golden all over. Meanwhile, cook the rice.

Turn the slow cooker to HIGH. Mix the rest of the cornflour with 2 tbsp cold water and stir it into the sauce along with the pineapple chunks. Cook for another 15–20 minutes until the sauce is glossy and thickened.
Only fold the tofu through just before serving, so the coating stays crispy. Sprinkle with spring onion (optional) and sesame seeds (optional) and serve with the rice.
tip: Buy firm tofu (tofu firme, in the chilled section with the vegetarian products). If you have time, press it under a heavy pan for 15 minutes: the drier it is, the crispier it gets. Taste the sauce at the end and make it sweeter with a teaspoon of sugar or fresher with a splash of vinegar.
kids: Crispy cubes in a pink sweet and sour sauce with pineapple: don't tell them it's tofu and let them guess what they're eating.

title: Swedish Meatballs in Cream Sauce
intro: Small, tender meatballs in a creamy gravy with nutmeg, with mash and sweet berry sauce: that Swedish IKEA feeling, but homemade.
steps: Mix the mince, egg, breadcrumbs, onion, nutmeg, salt and pepper and, with wet hands, roll into about 24 walnut-sized balls.
Brown the meatballs all over in hot oil in two batches; they don't need to be cooked through yet. Put them in the slow cooker.
Deglaze the pan with the stock and soy sauce, scrape up the browned bits and pour over the meatballs. Cook for 4–5 hours on LOW or 2–3 hours on HIGH.
Stir the cornflour into the cream until smooth and gently fold it into the sauce for the last 15 minutes. Let it thicken on HIGH.
Taste and season with salt and pepper. Serve with mash and a spoonful of berry sauce.
tip: You'll find lingonberry sauce at IKEA Málaga; cranberry sauce or a spoonful of forest fruit jam works just as well. Always brown mince first: raw mince heats up too slowly in the slow cooker.
kids: Let them help roll; with mash and sweet berry sauce, the meatballs vanish in no time.

title: Mexican Chicken Tortilla Soup
intro: A filling tomato soup with shredded chicken, beans and sweetcorn, with crunchy tortilla chips and toppings everyone chooses themselves.

ingredients.es: frijoles negros cocidos (Carrefour) of alubias rojas

steps: Put the onion, pepper, garlic, tomatoes, beans, sweetcorn (optional), cumin and paprika in the slow cooker. Lay the chicken on top and pour over the stock.
Don't fill the pot more than two-thirds full. Put the lid on and cook for 6–7 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH.
Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks and stir it back into the soup.
Season with lime juice, salt and pepper.
Ladle the soup into bowls and let everyone add their own tortilla chips, avocado, cheese and soured cream.
tip: Only add the chips to the bowl at the very last moment, or they go soggy. Put sliced jalapeño or hot sauce on the table separately for anyone who wants heat.
kids: Let them crumble chips into their soup and sprinkle cheese on top: a crunchy, soft treat.

title: Hungarian Chicken Paprikash with Soured Cream
intro: Tender chicken in a velvety paprika sauce, made creamy at the end with soured cream: the ultimate Hungarian grandma classic.
steps: Soften the onions in the oil for 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and paprika for just 30 seconds: burnt paprika turns bitter.
Spoon the onion mixture into the slow cooker with the peppers, tomatoes and stock. Add the chicken, season with salt and pepper and stir.
Put the lid on and cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH, until the chicken is tender and no longer pink inside.
Stir the flour into the soured cream until smooth and mix in a few spoonfuls of the hot sauce. Stir this into the pot for the last 15 minutes.
Let the sauce thicken slightly on HIGH, taste and season. Serve over tagliatelle.
tip: The flour in the soured cream stops the sauce splitting. Use ordinary sweet pimentón, not the smoked kind. Grown-ups can sprinkle a little pimentón picante over their plate at the table.
kids: Creamy pink sauce over pasta: cut the chicken small and it disappears in no time.

title: Provençal Chicken with Olives and Baby Potatoes
intro: Bone-in chicken thighs in tomato, garlic and herbes de Provence, with baby potatoes from the same pot: the South of France in one dish.
steps: Season the chicken with salt and pepper and brown it skin-side down in the oil for 5–6 minutes until golden; otherwise the skin stays flabby.
Put the baby potatoes, onion and pepper in the bottom of the slow cooker: potatoes cook more slowly than meat, so they belong at the hot bottom.
Pour over the tomatoes, stock, garlic and herbs and lay the chicken on top, skin-side up.
Put the lid on and cook for 6–7 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH, until the chicken comes away from the bone.
Stir in the olives (optional) for the last half hour. Grate over the lemon zest (optional), taste and season.
tip: Bone-in chicken stays extra juicy and copes fine with an extra hour. Want crispy skin? Pop the thighs under a hot oven grill for 5 minutes at the end.
kids: Fish out the olives for anyone who doesn't like them; baby potatoes in tomato sauce always go down well.

title: British Chicken and Leek Pie with a Puff Pastry Lid
intro: Creamy chicken with leek, carrot and mushrooms under a crisp puff pastry lid: a British pub classic, without the faff of a pie dish.
steps: Dust the chicken with flour, salt and pepper. Put it in the slow cooker with the leek, carrot, mushrooms (optional) and thyme.
Stir the mustard into the stock and pour over the chicken. Put the lid on and cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH.
Stir in the cream for the last 15 minutes and let the sauce thicken slightly on HIGH. Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Cut the puff pastry into 4 pieces, brush with egg (optional) and bake for 15–18 minutes until golden on a baking tray lined with baking paper.
Spoon the filling into deep plates and lay a puff pastry lid on each plate.
tip: A slow cooker lid traps steam, which is why you bake the pastry separately: that way it stays crisp. Leftover filling? Delicious over pasta or in a jacket potato.
kids: Let them cut out their own lid with a biscuit cutter; it tastes twice as good.

title: Moroccan Beef Tagine with Apricots
intro: Tender beef with cumin, cinnamon and sweet apricots, scattered with toasted almonds: a gently sweet tagine to serve with couscous.

ingredients.item: braising beef, cut into 4 cm chunks
ingredients.swap: boneless chicken thighs instead of beef

steps: Season the meat with salt and pepper and brown it all over in hot oil in two batches. Spoon it into the slow cooker.
Soften the onions in the same pan for 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic, ginger, cumin and cinnamon for 1 minute.
Deglaze with the tomatoes and stock, scrape up the browned bits and pour over the meat. Cook for 8–9 hours on LOW or 5–6 hours on HIGH.
Stir in the apricots for the last hour so they soften but don't fall apart.
Toast the almonds (optional) in a dry pan until golden, taste the tagine for salt and scatter over the almonds (optional).
tip: Couscous in five minutes: pour over an equal volume of boiling stock, cover, wait 5 minutes and fluff up with a fork and a knob of butter.
kids: Sweet apricots and cinnamon make it extra mild; stir the meat, finely shredded, through the couscous.

title: Lebanese Aubergine and Chickpea Stew
intro: Silky aubergine and chickpeas in a thick tomato sauce with cumin and cinnamon: Lebanese maghmour, warm or lukewarm with pitta.
steps: Brown the aubergine in the oil in two batches for 5–6 minutes; this makes it silky instead of grey and spongy.
Soften the onions in the same pan for 4 minutes and stir in the garlic, cumin and cinnamon for 1 minute.
Put everything in the slow cooker with the chickpeas, tomatoes, tomato purée, sugar and salt. Don't add any water: aubergine releases its own liquid.
Put the lid on and cook for 6–7 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH.
Taste, season and serve with yoghurt, mint and warm pitta.
tip: Maghmour is also delicious lukewarm or cold as a mezze, and tastes even better the next day. Put harissa or chilli flakes on the table separately.
kids: Mash it into a smooth dip and tear up some warm pitta for dipping.

title: Japanese Nikujaga with Beef and Potatoes
intro: Beef and potatoes in a sweet and savoury soy broth: Japanese home cooking that tastes as familiar as a Dutch beef stew.

ingredients.item: braising beef, cut into 2 cm dice
ingredients.swap: thinly sliced pork shoulder instead of beef

ingredients.item: waxy potatoes, cut into large chunks
carrots, cut into chunks on the diagonal

ingredients.es: salsa de soja baja en sal

steps: Fry the meat and onion in hot oil for 3–4 minutes until the meat is coloured all over.
Put the potatoes and carrots in the bottom of the slow cooker and spoon the meat and onion on top.
Mix the stock, soy sauce, sugar and mirin (optional) and pour it over. Cook for 7–8 hours on LOW or 4–5 hours on HIGH.
Optional: Lay the green beans on top for the last half hour and cook them on HIGH with the lid on until just tender.
Ladle everything into deep bowls with a generous spoonful of the sweet and salty broth.
tip: Nikujaga literally means 'meat and potatoes'. Choose waxy potatoes cut into large chunks so they hold their shape. No mirin in the house? An extra spoonful of sugar works too.
kids: Meat, potatoes and a sweet sauce: familiar enough for even the fussiest eater.

title: Sloppy Joes with Extra Vegetables
intro: Sweet and savoury mince in tomato sauce with plenty of hidden veg, on a toasted bun: a gloriously messy American treat that kids adore.

ingredients.swap: replace half the mince with red lentils

steps: Fry the mince in a hot pan until browned and crumbly and pour off the fat. Never put raw mince straight into the slow cooker: it clumps and heats up too slowly.
Fry the onion and pepper with it for 3 minutes and briefly stir in the garlic.
Spoon everything into the slow cooker with the carrot, passata, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce (optional), sugar, paprika, salt and pepper. Cook for 4–5 hours on LOW or 2–3 hours on HIGH.
Sauce too thin? Let it thicken on HIGH with the lid off for the last half hour.
Briefly toast the buns and pile a generous spoonful of mince on top.
tip: Leftovers are delicious over pasta or in a jacket potato. For the grown-ups: a few drops of Tabasco or some jalapeño on the table.
kids: Gloriously messy: give them a fork for everything that falls out of the bun.

title: Sauerkraut Stew with Smoked Sausage and Potato
intro: Dutch sauerkraut without the fuss: sauerkraut, potatoes and bacon cook until soft together, with apple to mellow it. Mash, add the sausage, done.

ingredients.item: Dutch smoked sausage or 4 smoked sausages

steps: Fry the bacon (optional) and onion in a frying pan for 5 minutes. Briefly rinse the sauerkraut if you want it less sour.
Put the potatoes in the bottom of the slow cooker. Spread the sauerkraut, apple (optional), bacon and onion and the bay leaf over the top and pour in the stock.
Cook for 6–7 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH, until the potatoes are completely soft.
Lay the sausage on top for the last half hour to warm through. Lift it out and fish out the bay leaf.
Mash the potato and sauerkraut with butter and warm milk into a creamy stamppot. Season and serve with slices of sausage.
tip: In Spain, sauerkraut is called chucrut: in jars at Lidl and Carrefour, sometimes at Mercadona. Taste it first; if it's very sour, rinse it in a colander under cold water.
kids: More potato, less sauerkraut and an extra slice of sausage: that way the sourness is easier for young tasters.

title: Hutspot with Braised Beef
intro: Leiden hutspot at its best: sweet carrot, onion and potato with butter-soft braised beef slowly cooking on top. Truly Dutch.

ingredients.item: beef thick flank or braising steaks, in 4 pieces
ingredients.es: falda o aguja de ternera para guisar
ingredients.swap: pork shoulder instead of beef

steps: Season the meat with salt and pepper and brown it all over in hot oil. Deglaze the pan with the stock.
Put the potato, carrot and onion in the bottom of the slow cooker, where it's hottest. Lay the meat and bay leaf on top and pour over the stock.
Cook for 8–9 hours on LOW or 5–6 hours on HIGH, until the meat falls apart.
Lift out the meat and bay leaf. Drain off the cooking liquid and keep it: that will be your gravy.
Mash the vegetables with butter, warm milk, nutmeg and a splash of the cooking liquid. Serve with the shredded meat and gravy.
tip: Spanish butchers don't know klapstuk: ask for falda or aguja para guisar, with a little fat on it. Lots of cooking liquid left? Boil it down in a saucepan into gravy.
kids: Hutspot is orange, soft and sweet: make a little well for the gravy and the plate will be empty in no time.

title: Coq au Vin-Light with Chicken Thighs
intro: French chicken in red wine sauce, made lighter and milder: chicken thighs, bacon, mushrooms and carrots. Also delicious with mosto tinto.

ingredients.item: bay leaves and a sprig of thyme

serve.item: tagliatelle with a knob of butter

steps: Fry the lardons (optional) until the fat runs and spoon them into the slow cooker. Dust the chicken with flour, salt and pepper and brown it in the bacon fat until golden.
Soften the shallots, carrot and garlic for 4 minutes, stir in the tomato purée and spoon everything into the slow cooker with the chicken.
Boil the wine hard in the pan for 5 minutes so most of the alcohol evaporates; mosto tinto only needs warming. Add the stock.
Pour this over the chicken, add the bay leaves and thyme and cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH.
Fry the mushrooms (optional) until golden and stir them in for the last half hour. Fish out the herbs and taste for salt and pepper.
tip: Bone-in chicken thighs give the richest sauce and stay juicy. Remove the skin: in the moist slow cooker it never goes crispy, just flabby.
kids: Pull the chicken off the bone over the tagliatelle. Cooking for children? Then choose mosto tinto.

title: Turkey Casserole with Apple, Cranberries and New Potatoes
intro: Tender turkey with new potatoes, apple and a hint of cranberry in a mild mustard gravy: a festive autumn casserole that's easy enough for a weeknight too.

ingredients.item: boneless turkey thigh, in 4 cm chunks

serve.item: boiled green beans or red cabbage

steps: Dust the turkey with flour, salt and pepper and brown it briefly all over in hot oil in two batches; that gives you flavour and a thickened sauce.
Put the potatoes and carrots (optional) in the bottom of the slow cooker, where it's hottest. Lay the turkey on top and scatter the onion and apple over it.
Deglaze the pan with the stock, stir in the mustard and scrape up the browned bits. Pour this into the slow cooker and add the thyme, bay leaf and cranberries (optional).
Put the lid on and cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3–3½ hours on HIGH, until the potatoes are soft and the turkey reaches at least 75 °C in the centre.

Fish out the thyme and bay leaf and turn to HIGH. Mix the cornflour smooth with the cooking cream (optional) or 3 tbsp cold water, stir it into the casserole and cook for another 15–20 minutes until the sauce thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
tip: Choose turkey thigh (contramuslo de pavo), not breast: thigh stays juicy during long cooking, while breast turns dry and stringy. No cranberries in the house? A tablespoon of redcurrant or blueberry jam in the sauce gives the same sweet-sharp touch.
kids: Soft little potatoes, sweet apple and mild gravy: mash it all together into a festive mash for little eaters.

title: Dutch Hunter's Pie with Apple and Mash
intro: Old-fashioned Dutch jachtschotel: braised beef with apple and onion in a gentle gravy, under a blanket of mash and cheese.

ingredients.item: braising beef, cut into 2 cm dice
ingredients.swap: pork shoulder instead of beef

ingredients.item: eating apples (Golden Delicious), cut into wedges

steps: Dust the meat with flour, salt and pepper and brown it in butter. Put it in the slow cooker with the onions.
Deglaze the pan with the stock and vinegar, scrape up the browned bits and pour over the meat. Add the bay leaf and cloves.
Cook for 7–8 hours on LOW or 4–5 hours on HIGH. Lay the apple wedges on top for the last hour so they don't fall apart.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes until tender and mash them with the milk, nutmeg, salt and pepper until smooth and creamy.
Fish out the bay leaf and cloves. Spoon the meat into an ovenproof dish, cover with the mash and cheese (optional) and brown under the grill for 10 minutes.
tip: Don't want to switch on the oven? Spread the mash over the meat in the slow cooker, sprinkle over the cheese and leave it on HIGH for another 20 minutes. Less crispy, just as tasty.
kids: Sweet apple, soft mash and melted cheese: let them dig out their own 'mountain with a surprise inside'.

title: Chicken Cacciatore with Peppers and Olives
intro: Italian hunter's chicken: chicken thighs in a mild tomato sauce with peppers, mushrooms and olives. Lovely with pasta or a hunk of bread.

ingredients.item: peppers (red and yellow), cut into strips

steps: Season the chicken with salt and pepper and brown it briefly in olive oil until golden. Optional, but it adds more flavour.
Put the onion, peppers and mushrooms (optional) in the slow cooker and lay the chicken on top.
Mix the garlic, chopped tomatoes, tomato purée, stock and herbs and pour over the chicken. Not much liquid: the vegetables release their own juices.
Cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3 hours on HIGH. Stir in the olives (optional) for the last half hour.
Pull the chicken into rough pieces if you like and taste for salt and pepper. Serve with pasta or bread.
tip: Traditionally a splash of wine goes in, but it barely reduces in the slow cooker. Still want that depth? Stir a teaspoon of balsamic vinegar into the sauce at the end.
kids: Halve the olives or leave them out; most children are happy with sweet peppers in tomato sauce.

title: Creamy Macaroni with Ham and Cheese
intro: Creamy macaroni with ham and cheese straight from the slow cooker: no separate sauce, no oven. Budget-friendly and always a hit.
steps: Grease the inner pot generously with butter. Add the macaroni, milk, cooking cream, water, mustard and nutmeg and stir well.
Cook for 2–2½ hours on LOW or 1–1½ hours on HIGH. Stir once halfway through so the macaroni doesn't stick to the sides.
Start tasting after 1 hour (HIGH) or 2 hours (LOW): the macaroni should be just al dente. Slow cookers vary, so keep a close eye on it the first time.
Stir in the cheese, ham and peas (optional) and leave for another 15 minutes with the lid on until everything is hot and creamy.
Too thick? Stir in a splash of warm milk. Season with pepper; salt is usually unnecessary thanks to the cheese and ham.
tip: This isn't a recipe to leave all day: pasta quickly goes mushy. Ideal for an afternoon at home. You'll find Gouda as queso gouda at Lidl and Mercadona.
kids: Kids' food through and through. Let them sprinkle on extra cheese and call the peas 'green pearls'.

title: Dutch Vegetable Soup with Meatballs
intro: Grandma's clear vegetable soup with tiny meatballs, vermicelli and plenty of vegetables. A bowl full of care and cosiness.
steps: Mix the mince, breadcrumbs, nutmeg, salt and pepper and, with wet hands, roll into marble-sized balls.
Put the leek, carrot, cauliflower (optional), celery and bay leaf in the slow cooker. Pour over the hot stock so everything comes up to temperature more quickly.
Gently slide the meatballs into the soup. Cook for 6–7 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH.
Switch to HIGH, break the vermicelli into pieces over the pot and stir. Cook for another 10–15 minutes with the lid on.
Fish out the bay leaf, skim any fat off the surface if needed and stir in the parsley (optional). Taste for salt.
tip: Want a clear soup? Boil the meatballs in water for 3 minutes first and pour away the frothy water. It freezes perfectly well, but without the vermicelli.
kids: Count the meatballs in each bowl together: everyone gets the same number, so no squabbles at the table.

title: Chicken Paprikash with Soured Cream
intro: Hungarian paprika chicken, kept gentle: chicken thighs in a velvety sauce of sweet paprika, onion and soured cream. Delicious with wide noodles.

ingredients.item: soured cream or full-fat Greek yoghurt
ingredients.es: nata agria o yogur griego natural

steps: Briefly brown the chicken in oil until golden and put it in the slow cooker. Soften the onions in the same pan for 5 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the paprika and garlic; that way the paprika doesn't burn and turn bitter.
Stir in the tomato purée and stock and pour over the chicken. Lay the pepper strips on top.
Cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3 hours on HIGH, until the chicken is tender.
Whisk the flour into the soured cream, stir in a little hot sauce and then stir it all into the stew. Another 15 minutes on HIGH.
tip: Choose pimentón dulce, not picante or ahumado: the sweet version is mild and gives the true paprikash colour. Only add dairy at the end, or it will split.
kids: Red sauce, tender chicken and wide noodles to slurp: cut the chicken small for the youngest ones.

title: Dutch Brown Bean Soup with Bacon
intro: Proper Dutch brown bean soup, thick and hearty with bacon and vegetables. Spanish judías pintas from a jar make perfect brown beans.

ingredients.item: brown beans (400 g each), with their liquid

steps: Fry the lardons for 5 minutes until the fat runs and soften the onion with them for 3 minutes. Stir in the tomato purée and curry powder and fry for a minute.
Put this in the slow cooker with the leek, carrot, celery, potato, bay leaf and stock. Add the beans with their liquid.
Cook for 6–7 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH.
Fish out the bay leaf. Blend half the soup with a stick blender so it thickens but still has some texture.
Taste and season with salt and pepper. Lovely with a slice of wholemeal bread and cheese.
tip: Jarred beans are already cooked and therefore safe. If you use dried beans, boil them hard for at least 10 minutes first: the slow cooker doesn't get hot enough for that.
kids: Blend their portion completely smooth and let them sprinkle croutons or grated cheese on top.

title: Mild Cauliflower and Potato Curry with Coconut
intro: Cauliflower and potatoes in a soft yellow coconut sauce with peas: a mild, creamy curry that children love straight away.

ingredients.item: waxy potatoes, cut into 2 cm dice

steps: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes. Stir in the curry powder and turmeric and fry for 1 minute; this brings the spices to life.
Put the potato in the bottom of the slow cooker and the cauliflower on top. Spoon over the onion mixture, tomatoes, coconut milk and stock.
Put the lid on and cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH, until the potato is cooked.
Stir in the frozen peas (optional) and let them warm through for 15 minutes with the lid on. Season with salt.
tip: Cut the cauliflower into large florets so they stay whole. A squeeze of lime and some fresh coriander just before serving make the curry lovely and fresh.
kids: Mash the potato and cauliflower with the sauce into the rice: mild, creamy and pale yellow.

title: Homemade Baked Beans on Toast
intro: White beans in a sweet, thick tomato sauce, far tastier than from a tin: British comfort food for breakfast or dinner.
steps: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes without letting them colour.
Put them in the slow cooker with the beans, passata, purée, sugar, vinegar, paprika and stock and stir well.
Put the lid on and cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3 hours on HIGH, until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Too thin? Leave the lid ajar for the last half hour. Season with salt, pepper and a little extra sugar or vinegar if needed.
tip: Jarred beans are already cooked and safe; the long, slow simmer lets them soak up all the sauce. Leftovers are at their best the next morning.
kids: Spoon the beans onto toast with a fried egg: an English breakfast for dinner.

title: Creamy Mushroom Stroganoff
intro: Fried mushrooms in a gentle paprika cream sauce: just as hearty and creamy as the meat original, but completely vegetarian.

ingredients.swap: ordinary button mushrooms only, no mixed mushrooms

steps: Fry the mushrooms in batches in the oil and butter until browned; this gives lots of flavour and no watery sauce.
Soften the onions and garlic in the same pan for 5 minutes. Stir in the paprika and purée and deglaze with the stock.
Put everything in the slow cooker. Put the lid on and cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3 hours on HIGH.
Switch to HIGH. Mix the cornflour with 2 tbsp cold water, stir it in and let it thicken for 15 minutes.
Switch off the slow cooker and only now stir in the crème fraîche, so it doesn't split. Sprinkle with parsley (optional).
tip: Mushrooms release a lot of liquid, so don't add any extra stock. Mix ordinary button mushrooms with a tub of setas for a deeper, almost meaty flavour.
kids: Lovely over rice or tagliatelle; slice the mushrooms a little finer for small eaters.

title: Creamy Risotto with Peas and Lemon
intro: Creamy risotto without the endless stirring: the slow cooker does the work, you just stir in the peas, lemon and cheese.
steps: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil and 1 tbsp butter for 5 minutes. Stir in the rice and fry for 1 minute until the grains turn translucent.
Put the rice in the slow cooker and pour in the hot stock. Stir well once.
Put the lid on and cook for 1½–2 hours on HIGH or 2½–3 hours on LOW, until the rice is almost cooked and creamy. Stir halfway through.
Stir in the peas and lemon zest and let them cook for 10 minutes with the lid on.
Switch off and stir in the cheese, the rest of the butter and a squeeze of lemon. Leave to rest for 2 minutes and serve straight away.
tip: Risotto is ready quickly in the slow cooker and goes mushy if it keeps cooking for too long: this isn't an all-day dish. Too thick? Stir in a little hot stock.
kids: Mild, creamy and with sweet peas; sprinkle on extra cheese for small eaters.

title: Shakshuka with Feta
intro: Eggs cooked in a gentle, fragrant tomato and pepper sauce: a festive breakfast-for-dinner with bread for dipping.
steps: Soften the onion and peppers in the oil for 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic, cumin and paprika and fry for 1 minute.
Put everything in the slow cooker with the tomatoes and sugar. Put the lid on and cook for 4–5 hours on LOW or 2–3 hours on HIGH.
Switch to HIGH and season the sauce. Use a spoon to make six little hollows and slide an egg into each one.
Put the lid on and cook for 20–30 minutes, until the whites are completely set. For young children, let the yolks firm up too.
Crumble over the feta (optional), sprinkle with parsley (optional) and carefully spoon out the eggs with the sauce.
tip: Crack each egg into a cup first so it slides into the sauce whole. Feel free to make double the sauce: without the eggs, it freezes perfectly.
kids: Give them baguette to dip into the tomato sauce, with a well-cooked egg on the side.

title: Salmon with Creamy Leeks and Baby Potatoes
intro: Baby potatoes and soft leeks cook for hours; the salmon steams for the last half hour on a creamy bed with lemon and dill.

ingredients.swap: frozen coley or hake instead of salmon

steps: Melt the butter and soften the leeks and garlic for 5 minutes. Put the baby potatoes in the bottom of the slow cooker and spoon the leeks on top.
Pour over the stock and season. Cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3 hours on HIGH, until the potatoes are tender.
Switch to HIGH. Stir the cream and mustard into the leeks. Lay the salmon on top and season with salt, pepper and lemon zest.
Put the lid on and cook for 30–40 minutes, until the salmon is just pale pink and flakes easily.
Sprinkle with dill (optional) and squeeze over some lemon. Serve the salmon, leeks and baby potatoes together.
tip: Defrost frozen salmon overnight in the fridge. Cooking cream copes better with heat than ordinary cream, so it doesn't split during that last half hour.
kids: Mash the salmon, baby potatoes and creamy leeks together; do check quickly for small bones.

title: Mild Fish Tacos with Pepper and Tomato Sauce
intro: White fish that cooks at the end in a gentle pepper and tomato sauce, in warm tortillas with crunchy coleslaw: a Friday night treat.

ingredients.item: white fish fillet (hake or cod), defrosted
ingredients.es: filetes de merluza o bacalao fresco
ingredients.swap: frozen pangasius instead of hake or cod

steps: Soften the onion, pepper and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes. Stir in the paprika and cumin and put everything in the slow cooker with the tomatoes.
Cook for 4–5 hours on LOW or 2–3 hours on HIGH, until the peppers are soft and the sauce is thick.
Switch to HIGH. Lay the fish in large pieces on the sauce, season with salt and lime zest and cook for 20–30 minutes with the lid on.
Pull the fish into rough pieces with two forks and gently fold it through the sauce. Squeeze over the lime juice.
Warm the tortillas briefly in a dry pan. Fill them with fish, sauce and a handful of coleslaw (optional).
tip: Fish is cooked as soon as it's opaque white and flakes easily; cooking it longer makes it dry. Defrost frozen fillets overnight in the fridge first.
kids: Let them build their own taco with fish, coleslaw, cheese and a spoonful of soured cream.

title: Apple and Cinnamon Breakfast Porridge
intro: Switch it on in the evening and wake up to warm, creamy porridge with apple and cinnamon: breakfast without the morning rush.
steps: Grease the inner pot generously with butter, especially at the bottom and around the sides: otherwise porridge quickly sticks.
Put the oats, milk, water, apple, raisins (optional), cinnamon and salt in the slow cooker and stir well.
Put the lid on and cook for 6–7 hours on LOW, for example overnight, or 2–2½ hours on HIGH.
Stir the porridge well and sweeten to taste with honey or sugar (optional). Too thick? Stir in a splash of warm milk.
tip: Jumbo oats hold their texture better than fine flakes during long cooking. If your slow cooker runs very hot, switch it to WARM after 5 hours. No honey for babies under 1 year.
kids: Let them choose their own toppings: banana, yoghurt or an extra pinch of cinnamon.

title: Slow Cooker Apple Crumble with Cinnamon
intro: Soft cinnamon apples under a buttery crumble topping, warm from the slow cooker: the easiest pudding for a Sunday afternoon.

ingredients.item: butter for greasing and kitchen paper

steps: Peel the apples, cut them into wedges and mix them in the greased slow cooker with the lemon juice, 2 tbsp sugar, cinnamon and cornflour.
Rub the flour, oats, the rest of the sugar and the cold butter together with your fingertips into coarse crumbs. Scatter them evenly over the apples.
Lay two layers of kitchen paper over the opening and put the lid on: that way the condensation won't drip onto your crumble.
Cook for 2–2½ hours on HIGH or 3½–4 hours on LOW, until the apples are soft and the juices bubble at the edges.
For a crunchier topping: leave the lid ajar for the last half hour. Serve warm with custard or ice cream.
tip: Crumble from the slow cooker is less crunchy than from the oven. So toast an extra handful of crumbs in a dry pan for 5 minutes and scatter them over when serving.
kids: Let them make the crumbs: rubbing butter and flour between your fingers is perfect work for children.

title: Slow Cooker Crème Caramel
intro: Silky Spanish caramel custard, cooked in a water bath in the slow cooker: no oven needed and guaranteed free of little holes.

ingredients.item: foil, kitchen paper and hot water

steps: Divide the caramel between the jars and stand them side by side on the bottom of the slow cooker.
Heat the milk with the lemon peel until just below boiling. Whisk the eggs, sugar and vanilla (optional) until smooth, without too much froth.
Pour the warm milk onto the eggs, stirring all the time. Strain the mixture, divide it between the jars and cover each jar with foil.
Pour hot water around the jars until it comes halfway up. Lay kitchen paper under the lid and cook for 2½–3 hours on LOW or 1½–2 hours on HIGH.
It's ready when the edge is firm and the centre still wobbles slightly. Leave to cool and set in the fridge for at least 4 hours.
tip: Too much heat causes little holes, so LOW is the better choice. Turning them out? Run a small knife around the edge, put a saucer on top and flip it over in one quick movement.
kids: Let them turn the flans out themselves: caramel running down the flan is always a wow moment.

title: Slow Cooker Farmhouse Loaf
intro: A round farmhouse loaf with a soft crumb, baked without an oven: ideal on hot summer days. This recipe makes 1 loaf of approx. 800 g (about 16 slices).

ingredients.item: baking paper and a clean tea towel

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a large bowl. Add the water and oil and knead for 10 minutes into a smooth, slightly sticky dough (6 minutes in a stand mixer).
Cover and leave to rise in a warm place for about 1 hour, until the dough has doubled in size. On the Costa in summer, this often takes just 45 minutes.
Press the dough flat and fold it into a tight ball. Put the ball on a piece of baking paper, brush with water and sprinkle with the seeds (optional). Cut a cross in the top.

Lift the ball into the slow cooker by the baking paper. Stretch a clean tea towel tightly over the pot, fold the corners up onto the lid (away from the hot outer wall) and put the lid on. Bake for 2–2½ hours on HIGH.

The bread is ready when the base is golden brown and sounds hollow when tapped (core temperature approx. 95 °C). Want a brown top? 3–5 minutes under the grill or in the air fryer at 200 °C. Leave to cool on a wire rack.
tip: Buy 'levadura seca de panadería', not 'levadura química': that's baking powder. The tea towel catches the condensation; otherwise it drips onto the bread and the top turns soggy. An oval 4.5–6 litre pot works best. Every slow cooker is different, so check after 1¾ hours.
kids: Let the children help knead and roll little rolls. They're done after about 1½ hours on HIGH.

title: Slow Cooker Banana Bread
intro: Moist banana bread that bakes itself while you head to the beach: the best destination for overripe bananas. This recipe makes 1 loaf of about 10 slices.

ingredients.item: loaf tin (approx. 22 x 10 cm), baking paper, foil and a tea towel

steps: First check that the loaf tin fits in the slow cooker with the lid closed. Grease it and line it with baking paper. No tin that fits? Line the pot itself with baking paper, leaving flaps sticking up.
Mash the bananas with a fork. Whisk in the eggs, melted butter, sugar and vanilla (optional).

Mix the flour, baking powder, salt and cinnamon (optional) and briefly fold this into the banana mixture. Don't stir any longer than necessary. Finally, fold in the walnuts or chocolate chips (optional).

Pour the batter into the tin. Stand the tin in the slow cooker on three balls of foil so the heat can circulate all around it. Lay a tea towel under the lid and bake for 2–2½ hours on HIGH or 3½–4 hours on LOW.
It's ready when a skewer in the centre comes out clean; start checking after 2 hours. Leave to rest in the tin for 10 minutes, then cool on a wire rack.
tip: The browner the bananas, the sweeter and moister the bread. No time right now? Freeze ripe bananas without their skins and defrost them later. The top stays paler than when baked in the oven; that's how it should be.
kids: Let them mash the bananas and sprinkle over the chocolate chips themselves.

title: Rosemary and Olive Oil Focaccia
intro: Airy focaccia with a crisp, olive-oil-rich base, with no kneading and no oven. This recipe makes 1 focaccia, enough for 8 pieces with a salad or with drinks.

ingredients.item: baking paper and a clean tea towel

steps: Mix the flour, yeast and salt in a bowl. Stir in the water and 2 tbsp oil to make a sticky dough; no kneading needed. Cover and leave to rise for 1½ hours, until the dough is full of bubbles.
Line the slow cooker with a large sheet of baking paper that comes halfway up the sides and pour 2 tbsp oil onto it.
Tip the dough onto the baking paper and press it out to the edges with oiled fingers. Leave it to rise for another 30 minutes with the lid on and the slow cooker switched off.
Press deep dimples into the dough with your fingertips. Drizzle over the last of the oil and scatter over the rosemary and tomatoes (optional).

Lay a tea towel under the lid and bake for 1½–2 hours on HIGH, until the base is golden brown and crisp. Lift the focaccia out by the baking paper, sprinkle with sea salt (optional) and colour the top under the grill for 3–5 minutes if you like.
tip: The dough is very wet; that's exactly what creates the big air holes. Don't set the slow cooker to WARM while it rises: at over 70 °C that setting is too hot and kills the yeast. Dried rosemary (1 tsp) works too.
kids: Let them press in the dimples with their fingers and make a little face out of tomatoes and olives.

title: Homemade Yoghurt
intro: Creamy, mild yoghurt for a fraction of the shop price. After heating, it rests overnight wrapped in a towel. This recipe makes approx. 2 litres.

ingredients.item: natural yoghurt with live cultures (1 pot)
sieve with muslin or a clean tea towel (for Greek yoghurt)

steps: Pour the milk into the slow cooker, put the lid on and heat for 2½–3 hours on LOW, until the milk reaches approx. 82 °C. This heating makes the yoghurt thicker.

Switch off the slow cooker and unplug it. Let the milk cool with the lid on for 2½–3 hours to approx. 43 °C (40–45 °C). Really do measure it: above 46 °C the bacteria die, below 38 °C they don't become active.
Ladle a cup of the lukewarm milk into a bowl, stir in the yoghurt until smooth and gently stir this back into the milk in the pot.
Put the lid on, wrap the whole slow cooker in a thick bath towel or blanket and leave it undisturbed for 8–12 hours in a draught-free spot, unplugged. The longer, the thicker and tangier.
Put the yoghurt in the fridge for at least 4 hours to set. Want Greek yoghurt? Let it drain for 1–2 hours in a sieve lined with muslin (optional).
tip: Choose a pot labelled 'yogur': in Spain, that has to contain live cultures. A 'postre lácteo' won't work. Save 2 tbsp of your own yoghurt as a starter for next time; after 4–5 rounds, buy a fresh pot. It keeps for 1–2 weeks in the fridge. In summer, a thin towel is often all you need.
kids: Set up a yoghurt buffet with fruit, granola and a little honey (honey only from 1 year).

title: Clear Chicken Stock
intro: Golden, rich stock from chicken carcasses that simmers away by itself while you sleep: the base for soups, risotto and sauces. This recipe makes approx. 2 litres.
steps: Put the carcasses or wings in the slow cooker with the onion, carrot, celery, garlic, bay leaves and peppercorns. Add the leek, parsley stalks and vinegar (optional).
Pour in cold water until everything is just covered, but stay 3 cm below the rim.
Put the lid on and cook for 10–12 hours on LOW or 5–6 hours on HIGH. Don't stir, so the stock stays clear. Skim off any foam after the first hour if needed.
Lift out the bones and vegetables and strain the stock through a fine sieve. Don't add salt yet; only do that when you use the stock.

Divide the stock between shallow containers and put it in the fridge within 2 hours. The next day the fat will have set in a firm layer on top: skim it off. Keeps for 4 days in the fridge and 3 months in the freezer.
tip: Mercadona often sells chicken carcasses ('carcasas de pollo') or a soup pack ('preparado para caldo') for a few euros. When cold, the stock turns jelly-like; that's a good sign. Freeze it in 250 ml portions or in an ice cube tray.
kids: Cook star pasta in it or use it for a classic chicken soup with little meatballs.

title: Fresh Vegetable Stock
intro: A fragrant, full-flavoured vegetable stock without packets or cubes, also lovely made with your saved vegetable scraps. This recipe makes approx. 2 litres.

ingredients.item: parsley and a few sprigs of thyme

steps: Put the onion, carrot, celery, leek and garlic in the slow cooker. Add the mushrooms, tomato and herbs (optional), together with the bay leaves and peppercorns.
Pour in the water and stir in the soy sauce (optional). Leave 3 cm of space below the rim.
Put the lid on and cook for 8–10 hours on LOW or 4–5 hours on HIGH.
Strain the stock, pressing the vegetables lightly. Only season with salt when you use the stock.
Cool the stock quickly in shallow containers and put it in the fridge (keeps for 5 days) or the freezer (3 months).
tip: For a week, save peelings and scraps of onion, carrot, leek, celery and mushrooms in a bag in the freezer, then turn them into stock. Don't use cabbage, broccoli or potato peelings: they make the stock bitter or cloudy. Want a dark stock? First char the onions cut-side down in a dry pan.
kids: Use it as the base for a mild vegetable soup with vermicelli (fideos).

title: Old-Fashioned Apple Sauce
intro: Soft, fresh apple sauce just like it used to be, without anything catching on the bottom. You decide how much sugar goes in. This recipe makes approx. 1.2 litres, enough for 6 jars.

ingredients.item: apples, ideally a mix (e.g. Golden Delicious and Reineta)

steps: Peel the apples, remove the cores and cut them into large chunks.
Put the apples in the slow cooker with the water or apple juice and the lemon juice. Add the cinnamon stick (optional).
Put the lid on and cook for 5–6 hours on LOW or 3 hours on HIGH, until the apples fall apart.
Remove the cinnamon stick. Mash the apples coarsely with a potato masher or blend them smooth with a stick blender. Stir in sugar (optional) to taste.
Leave the apple sauce to cool and spoon it into clean jars. Keeps for 1 week in the fridge and 6 months in the freezer.
tip: Reineta apples collapse into a lovely light, fluffy sauce and are pleasantly tart. Golden Delicious is sweeter, so you often won't need sugar. If you use a stick blender, there's no need to peel the apples; the skin gives a pink tinge and extra fibre.
kids: Without sugar, this is a great food from 6 months. Freeze small portions in an ice cube tray.

title: Caramelised Onions
intro: Deep golden, sweet onions without standing at the hob for an hour, for tortilla, burgers, onion soup or a tosta with goat's cheese. This recipe makes approx. 500 g, enough for 2 jars.

ingredients.item: onions (8–10 large), cut into ½ cm half-moons

steps: Put the onions in the slow cooker; the pot can be completely full, as they shrink enormously. Scatter over the butter, oil, salt, sugar and thyme (optional) and toss everything together.
Put the lid on and cook for 10–12 hours on LOW. Toss once halfway through if you're around.

Are the onions soft but is there still a lot of liquid in the pot? Then wedge a wooden spoon between the pot and the lid and cook for another 1–2 hours on HIGH, until the liquid has evaporated and the onions are deep golden and jammy. Stir now and then.
Optional: Stir in the sherry vinegar for a fresh, sweet-and-sour finish.
Leave the onions to cool and spoon them into clean jars. Keeps for 1 week in the fridge. Freeze the rest in portions in an ice cube tray.
tip: A mandoline or food processor saves a lot of tears. Open a window: the house will smell of onions all day. A tablespoon of onions stirred through a tortilla de patatas instantly makes it 'con cebolla caramelizada'.
kids: Mix a spoonful into mince for burgers: lovely and sweet, and the onion is invisible.

title: Chickpeas from Dried with Creamy Hummus
intro: In the slow cooker, dried chickpeas turn butter-soft and far tastier than tinned, perfect for the smoothest hummus. This recipe makes approx. 1.2 kg of cooked chickpeas: 300 g goes into a big bowl of hummus, and you keep the rest.

ingredients.item: bay and garlic for the cooking water
sweet paprika and a drizzle of oil on top

steps: Rinse the chickpeas and pick out any little stones. Soaking isn't necessary, but if you soak them for 8–12 hours they cook more quickly and evenly.

Put the chickpeas in the slow cooker with hot water; the water should come 5 cm above them. Add the bicarbonate of soda, bay leaf and garlic (optional). Don't add lemon or tomato yet: acid keeps them hard.

Put the lid on and cook unsoaked for 8–10 hours on LOW or 4–5 hours on HIGH (soaked: 6–8 hours on LOW or 3–4 hours on HIGH). They're done when you can easily squash one between your fingers. Stir in the salt and leave them in the cooking liquid for 15 minutes.

For the hummus, blend 300 g warm chickpeas with the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, oil, a pinch of salt and the ice-cold water for 3–4 minutes until smooth, in a blender or with a stick blender. Taste and add more lemon or water if needed.

Spoon the hummus into a bowl and finish with paprika and a drizzle of oil (optional). Leave the rest of the chickpeas to cool in their cooking liquid: they keep for 4–5 days in the fridge, or 3 months in the freezer in portions with a little liquid.
tip: This only works with chickpeas, lentils and other safe pulses. Never put dried red kidney beans raw into the slow cooker: they must be boiled hard for 10 minutes first, or they can make you seriously ill. The cooking liquid (aquafaba) can be whipped as a substitute for egg white. You'll find tahini among the international products or at Lidl.
kids: Hummus with cucumber and carrot sticks or pitta bread is a much-loved dip; leave out the garlic for the little ones if you like.

title: Slow Cooker Jacket Potatoes
intro: Fluffy, creamy jacket potatoes that are ready when you get home, without the oven being on for hours. This recipe is for 4 large potatoes, serving 4 as a lunch or side dish.
steps: Scrub the potatoes clean, pat them dry and prick the skin all over 6–8 times with a fork.
Rub them with the oil and coarse salt. Lay a sheet of baking paper on the bottom of the slow cooker and arrange the potatoes on it side by side. Don't add any water.
Put the lid on and cook for 7–8 hours on LOW or 4–5 hours on HIGH, until a skewer slides through the centre with no resistance.
Want a crispy skin? Put the potatoes in the air fryer or the oven at 220 °C for another 10 minutes.
Cut a cross in the top, squeeze the potato open and add a knob of butter. Finish with cheese, yoghurt and spring onion (optional).
tip: Choose a floury variety such as Agria or Kennebec ('patata para asar' or 'para freír'). If you wrap them in foil, the skin turns softer and they stay warm for longer on the keep-warm setting. Leftovers? Mash them the next day into fried potato cakes.
kids: Set up a filling bar with cheese, sweetcorn, ham and yoghurt so everyone can fill their own potato.

title: Creamy Hot Chocolate
intro: Velvety hot chocolate made with real chocolate, kept ready on the keep-warm setting for a birthday, a cold evening or Three Kings' Day. This recipe makes approx. 1.5 litres, about 6 mugs.

ingredients.swap: 2 tbsp extra cocoa and sugar instead of chocolate

steps: In the slow cooker, whisk the cocoa powder, sugar and salt with a splash of milk until smooth, so there are no lumps.
Stir in the rest of the milk, the cream (optional) and the chocolate and add the cinnamon stick (optional).
Put the lid on and heat for 2–2½ hours on LOW or 1–1½ hours on HIGH. Whisk well after 30 minutes and then every half hour, until all the chocolate has melted. Don't let it boil.
Remove the cinnamon stick and stir in the vanilla (optional). On the keep-warm setting, the hot chocolate stays lovely for up to 2 hours; stir now and then.
Optional: Pour into mugs and top with whipped cream and marshmallows.
tip: Want Spanish 'chocolate a la taza' for dunking churros? Mix 2 tbsp cornflour with a splash of cold milk and whisk it in during the last half hour: it turns lovely and thick. A bar of Valor 'chocolate a la taza' works too.
kids: Set up a topping bar with marshmallows, sprinkles and whipped cream; give the little ones half a mug topped up with extra milk.

title: Strawberry Jam with Lemon
intro: Fresh jam made with Huelva strawberries, slowly thickening in the slow cooker with no splattering and no burning. This recipe makes approx. 750 ml, enough for 3 jars of 250 ml.

ingredients.item: green apple, peeled and finely grated (natural pectin)

steps: Wash and hull the strawberries and halve them. Put them in the slow cooker with the sugar, lemon juice and grated apple. Stir and leave for 30 minutes, until the strawberries release their juice.
Put the lid on and heat for 1 hour on HIGH, until the sugar has completely dissolved. Stir well.

Wedge a wooden spoon between the pot and the lid so moisture can escape. Cook for another 3–4 hours on HIGH, stirring every hour. Mash the strawberries halfway through with a potato masher if you want a smoother jam.

Do the saucer test: put a teaspoon of jam on a saucer from the freezer and wait 1 minute. If the jam wrinkles when you push it with your finger, it's ready. Still too runny? Cook it for another 30–60 minutes, or boil it hard for 3–5 minutes in a pan on the hob. Stir in the vanilla (optional).

Rinse the jars with boiling water and fill them with the hot jam. Screw the lids on straight away. Keep the jam in the fridge: that way it stays good for 4–6 weeks. It keeps for 1 year in the freezer.
tip: A slow cooker doesn't get above 95 °C, so the jam turns out a little softer than jam made in a pan. The grated apple and the saucer test take care of the set. Want it guaranteed firm? Use 'azúcar especial para mermeladas' (jam sugar). Outside the season (February–June), frozen strawberries work just as well.
kids: On a fresh slice of slow cooker farmhouse loaf (recipe 111), this is a real treat.
